body: A unified rendering function that dispatches to specific Gaussian rasterizers (3DGS, 2DGS, or GGGS) based on the model's scale dimensions or explicit mode flag, handling data preparation (means, opacities, SHs) and post-processing of rasterizer outputs (depth, normals, alpha). It abstracts the backend selection logic, allowing a single entry point to support multiple Gaussian splatting variants by inspecting the input Gaussian properties or configuration flags. Inputs: pc: A Gaussian point cloud object containing attributes: means (3D positions), opacities (scalar opacities), scales (log-scales or scales), rotations (quaternions), harmonic/features (SH coefficients), maxshdegree. viewpointcamera: Camera object with FoVx, FoVy, viewmatrix, projmatrix, campos. pipe: Configuration object with flags computecov3Dpython, convertSHspython, depthratio. gsmode: Optional explicit mode string ("3DGS", "2DGS", "GGGS"). overridecolor: Optional tensor to bypass SH computation. batchidx: Indices to select specific Gaussians from pc. Outputs: render: Color image tensor. depth: Depth map tensor (format depends on mode). alpha: Alpha mask tensor. normal: Normal map tensor (2DGS/GGGS only). Data Structures: GaussianRasterizationSettings: A configuration struct passed to the rasterizer constructor. Fields: imageheight, imagewidth, tanfovx, tanfovy, bg (background color), scalingmodifier, viewmatrix, projmatrix, shdegree, campos, prefiltered, debug. For GGGS, additional fields: kernelsize, sgdegree, requiredepth. GaussianRasterizer: The backend instance. Variants: diffsurfelrasterization (2DGS), diffgaussianrasterization (3DGS), gggsdiffgaussianrasterization (GGGS). Steps: 1. Extract Batch Attributes: Select Gaussian attributes for the current batch: \text{xyz} = \text{pc.means}[\text{batch\idx}] \text{opacity} = \text{pc.opacities}[\text{batch\idx}].\text{unsqueeze}(-1) 2. Initialize Screenspace Points: Create a zero tensor for screen-space points to capture gradients: \text{screenspace\points} = \text{torch.zeros}(\text{xyz.shape}, \text{dtype}=\text{xyz.dtype}, \text{requires\grad}=\text{True}, \text{device}=\text{"cuda"}) The + 0 in the source ensures the tensor is on the correct device and dtype. 3. Compute Tangent FOV: \text{tanfovx} = \tan(\text{viewpoint\camera.FoVx} \times 0.5) \text{tanfovy} = \tan(\text{viewpoint\camera.FoVy} \times 0.5) 4. Determine Render Mode: If gsmode is explicitly set, use it. Otherwise, infer from pc.scales: If pc.scales[batchidx].shape[1] == 2, set requestedrendermode = "2DGS". Else, set requestedrendermode = "3DGS". GGGS mode is typically selected via explicit gsmode or specific attribute checks not detailed in the scale dimension logic. 5. Select Rasterizer Classes: Map requestedrendermode to the appropriate GaussianRasterizationSettings and GaussianRasterizer classes: "2DGS": diffsurfelrasterization "3DGS": diffgaussianrasterization "GGGS": gggsdiffgaussianrasterization 6. Construct Settings: Initialize GaussianRasterizationSettings with: imageheight, imagewidth tanfovx, tanfovy bg (background color) scalingmodifier viewmatrix, projmatrix shdegree campos prefiltered=False debug For GGGS, additionally pass kernelsize, sgdegree=0, requiredepth. 7. Prepare Covariance: If pipe.computecov3Dpython is true: Compute world-space covariance from scales and rotations. Transform to pixel space using ndc2pix and world2pix matrices. Reshape to (-1, 9) in column-major order. Else: Set scales and rotations directly from pc. 8. Prepare Colors: If overridecolor is None and pipe.convertSHspython is true: Extract SH features: shsview = pc.getfeatures.transpose(1, 2).view(-1, 3, (pc.maxshdegree+1)2) Compute viewing directions: dirpp (from camera to point), normalize: dirppnormalized = dirpp / dirpp.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True) Evaluate SH: sh2rgb = evalsh(pc.activeshdegree, shsview, dirppnormalized) Clamp: colorsprecomp = torch.clampmin(sh2rgb + 0.5, 0.0) Else: Set shs = pc.harmonics[batchidx].permute(0, 2, 1) 9. Execute Rasterizer: Call the selected rasterizer with: means3D: xyz means2D: screenspacepoints shs: SH coefficients (if not precomputed) colorsprecomp: Precomputed colors (if SH conversion used) opacity scales rotations cov3Dprecomp For GGGS, also pass sgaxis, sgsharpness, sgcolor. 10. Post-process 2DGS Outputs: Extract from allmap: renderalpha = allmap[1:2] rendernormal = allmap[2:5] (transform to world space) renderdepthmedian = allmap[5:6] renderdepthexpected = allmap[0:1] / renderalpha renderdist = allmap[6:7] Compute surface depth: \text{surf\depth} = \text{render\depth\expected} \times (1 - \text{pipe.depth\ratio}) + \text{pipe.depth\ratio} \times \text{render\depth\median} Compute surface normal: \text{surf\normal} = \text{depth\to\normal}(\text{viewpoint\camera}, \text{surf\depth}) \times \text{render\alpha.detach()} 11. Post-process 3DGS Outputs: Compute depth from inverse depth: \text{depth} = 1.0 / \text{inv\depth.clamp(min=1e-6)} 12. Post-process GGGS Outputs: Retrieve optional attributes sgaxis, sgsharpness, sgcolor from pc (handling defaults and tensor dimensions). Return renderedmediandepth, renderedalpha, renderednormal. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math import torch def unifiedgaussiansplattingdispatch(pc, viewpointcamera, pipe, gsmode=None, overridecolor=None, batchidx=None): # 1. Extract Batch Attributes if batchidx is None: batchidx = slice(None) xyz = pc.means[batchidx] opacity = pc.opacities[batchidx].unsqueeze(-1) # 2. Initialize Screenspace Points screenspacepoints = torch.zeroslike(xyz, dtype=xyz.dtype, requiresgrad=True, device="cuda") # 3. Compute Tangent FOV tanfovx = math.tan(viewpointcamera.FoVx 0.5) tanfovy = math.tan(viewpointcamera.FoVy 0.5) # 4. Determine Render Mode if gsmode is not None: requestedrendermode = gsmode else: # Check scale dimensions to infer mode scales = pc.scales[batchidx] if scales.shape[1] == 2: requestedrendermode = "2DGS" else: requestedrendermode = "3DGS" # 5. Select Rasterizer Classes if requestedrendermode == "2DGS": from diffsurfelrasterization import GaussianRasterizationSettings as RasterizationSettings2D from diffsurfelrasterization import GaussianRasterizer as Rasterizer2D elif requestedrendermode == "GGGS": from gggsdiffgaussianrasterization import GaussianRasterizationSettings as RasterizationSettingsGGGS from gggsdiffgaussianrasterization import GaussianRasterizer as RasterizerGGGS else: # 3DGS from diffgaussianrasterization import GaussianRasterizationSettings as RasterizationSettings3D from diffgaussianrasterization import GaussianRasterizer as Rasterizer3D # 6. Construct Settings settingskwargs = { "imageheight": viewpointcamera.imageheight, "imagewidth": viewpointcamera.imagewidth, "tanfovx": tanfovx, "tanfovy": tanfovy, "bg": pipe.bg, # Assuming pipe has bg attribute "scalingmodifier": pipe.scalingmodifier, "viewmatrix": viewpointcamera.viewmatrix, "projmatrix": viewpointcamera.projmatrix, "shdegree": pc.activeshdegree, "campos": viewpointcamera.campos, "prefiltered": False, "debug": False } if requestedrendermode == "GGGS": settingskwargs.update({ "kernelsize": pipe.kernelsize, "sgdegree": 0, "requiredepth": True }) if requestedrendermode == "2DGS": settings = RasterizationSettings2D(settingskwargs) rasterizer = Rasterizer2D(rasterizersettings=settings) elif requestedrendermode == "GGGS": settings = RasterizationSettingsGGGS(settingskwargs) rasterizer = RasterizerGGGS(rasterizersettings=settings) else: settings = RasterizationSettings3D(settingskwargs) rasterizer = Rasterizer3D(rasterizersettings=settings) # 7. Prepare Covariance if pipe.computecov3Dpython: # Compute cov3Dprecomp from scales and rotations # Transform world-space covariance to pixel space # Reshape to (-1, 9) column-major cov3Dprecomp = computecov3Dpython(pc, batchidx) # Helper function not detailed in source else: cov3Dprecomp = None scales = pc.scales[batchidx] rotations = pc.rotations[batchidx] # 8. Prepare Colors if overridecolor is None and pipe.convertSHspython: shsview = pc.getfeatures.transpose(1, 2).view(-1, 3, (pc.maxshdegree+1)2) dirpp = xyz - viewpointcamera.campos dirppnormalized = dirpp / dirpp.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True) sh2rgb = evalsh(pc.activeshdegree, shsview, dirppnormalized) colorsprecomp = torch.clampmin(sh2rgb + 0.5, 0.0) shs = None else: colorsprecomp = overridecolor shs = pc.harmonics[batchidx].permute(0, 2, 1) # 9. Execute Rasterizer if requestedrendermode == "GGGS": sgaxis = pc.sgaxis[batchidx] if hasattr(pc, 'sgaxis') else None sgsharpness = pc.sgsharpness[batchidx] if hasattr(pc, 'sgsharpness') else None sgcolor = pc.sgcolor[batchidx] if hasattr(pc, 'sgcolor') else None renderout = rasterizer( means3D=xyz, means2D=screenspacepoints, shs=shs, colorsprecomp=colorsprecomp, opacity=opacity, scales=scales, rotations=rotations, cov3Dprecomp=cov3Dprecomp, sgaxis=sgaxis, sgsharpness=sgsharpness, sgcolor=sgcolor) else: renderout = rasterizer( means3D=xyz, means2D=screenspacepoints, shs=shs, colorsprecomp=colorsprecomp, opacity=opacity, scales=scales, rotations=rotations, cov3Dprecomp=cov3Dprecomp) # 10, 11, 12. Post-process if requestedrendermode == "2DGS": allmap = renderout renderalpha = allmap[1:2] rendernormal = allmap[2:5] # Transform normal to world space renderdepthmedian = allmap[5:6] renderdepthexpected = allmap[0:1] / renderalpha renderdist = allmap[6:7] surfdepth = renderdepthexpected (1 - pipe.depthratio) + pipe.depthratio renderdepthmedian surfnormal = depthtonormal(viewpointcamera, surfdepth) renderalpha.detach() return renderout[0:3], surfdepth, renderalpha, surfnormal elif requestedrendermode == "3DGS": invdepth = renderout[0] # Assuming first channel is inverse depth depth = 1.0 / invdepth.clamp(min=1e-6) return renderout[1:4], depth, renderout[0:1], None else: # GGGS renderedmediandepth = renderout.mediandepth renderedalpha = renderout.alpha renderednormal = renderout.normal return renderout.color, renderedmediandepth, renderedalpha, renderednormal def computecov3Dpython(pc, batchidx): # Placeholder for covariance computation logic # Transform world-space covariance to pixel space using ndc2pix and world2pix # Reshape to (-1, 9) column-major pass def evalsh(deg, shs, dirs): # Placeholder for SH evaluation pass def depthtonormal(cam, depth): # Placeholder for normal computation from depth pass Prepares a dictionary of PyTorch tensors containing 3D Gaussian parameters filtered by timestep, formatted for the differentiable Gaussian rasterizer. It converts raw learnable parameters (log-scales, logit-opacities, unnormalized rotations) into the physical quantities required by the rasterization kernel (scales, opacities, normalized rotations). It also initializes the 2D mean positions and constructs separate variable sets for color rendering and depth/silhouette rendering. Time Complexity: Dominated by the rasterization backend (3DGS, 2DGS, or GGGS). The dispatch and data preparation steps are O(N) where N is the number of Gaussians. Memory Complexity: O(N) for storing Gaussian attributes and intermediate tensors (screenspace points, precomputed colors/covariances). Performance: Depends on the selected backend. 2DGS may offer better normal estimation but requires more complex post-processing. GGGS adds overhead for spherical Gaussian parameters. Strengths: Unified interface for multiple Gaussian splatting variants; automatic mode selection based on geometry; handles SH conversion and covariance computation flexibly. Limitations: Requires careful handling of different backend APIs; post-processing logic varies significantly between modes; potential for precision issues in depth computation (e.g., division by alpha). When to use: When supporting multiple Gaussian splatting variants (3DGS, 2DGS, GGGS) in a single codebase or when the mode is determined dynamically by input data. When not to use: When only one specific variant is needed and performance is critical (direct backend call avoids dispatch overhead). It abstracts the differences between 3DGS, 2DGS, and GGGS rasterizers to provide a consistent interface for rendering Gaussian primitives. body: This method prepares the input data structures required by the differentiable Gaussian rasterizer kernel. It filters raw Gaussian parameters by a specified timestep, normalizes and converts latent representations (logits, logs) into physical attributes (opacities, scales), and packages them into a dictionary (rendervar) compatible with the CUDA backend. It distinguishes itself by handling temporal filtering and specific tensor shape adjustments (such as tiling single-dimension scales) before the rasterization call, ensuring the kernel receives correctly formatted and normalized data. Inputs: params: A dictionary containing raw Gaussian parameters. Key fields include timestep (integer/float), logscales (tensor), logitopacities (tensor), unnormrotations (tensor), rgbcolors (tensor), and means3D (tensor). currtimestep: The current time step index used for filtering. w2c: World-to-camera transformation matrix (required only for depth rendering variant). Outputs: rendervar: A dictionary of PyTorch tensors formatted for standard color rendering. depthrendervar: A dictionary of PyTorch tensors formatted for depth/silhouette rendering. Data Structures: The output is a Python dictionary (rendervar) with the following keys: means3D: 3D mean positions of Gaussians. colorsprecomp: Pre-computed colors (RGB). rotations: Normalized rotation quaternions. opacities: Scalar opacity values. scales: Log-scaled dimensions. means2D: 2D projected means, initialized to zeros. Steps: 1. Temporal Filtering: Identify active Gaussians by filtering params['timestep'] where the value is less than or equal to currtimestep. Use boolean indexing to extract the subset of parameters, resulting in selectedparams. 2. Scale Tiling: Check the last dimension of selectedparams['logscales']. If the size is 1, tile this dimension to 3 using torch.tile to match the expected 3D scale format. 3. Opacity Conversion: Compute final opacities by applying the sigmoid function to selectedparams['logitopacities']: \text{opacities} = \sigma(\text{logit\opacities}) 4. Scale Conversion: Compute final scales by applying the exponential function to the (possibly tiled) logscales: \text{scales} = \exp(\text{log\scales}) 5. Rotation Normalization: Normalize the unnormrotations using L2 normalization to ensure valid unit quaternions: \text{rotations} = \frac{\text{unnorm\rotations}}{\|\text{unnorm\rotations}\|2} 6. Means2D Initialization: Create a zero tensor on the CUDA device with the same shape as means3D to serve as the placeholder for 2D projected means. 7. Construct rendervar: Assemble the dictionary with keys means3D, colorsprecomp (taken from rgbcolors), rotations, opacities, scales, and means2D. 8. Construct depthrendervar: Assemble a similar dictionary, but replace colorsprecomp with the output of a helper function getdepthandsilhouette(selectedparams['means3D'], w2c). Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import torch import torch.nn.functional as F def preparegaussianvariables(params, currtimestep, w2c=None): # 1. Filter by timestep mask = params['timestep'] <= currtimestep selectedparams = {k: v[mask] for k, v in params.items()} # 2. Handle scale dimension logscales = selectedparams['logscales'] if logscales.shape[-1] == 1: logscales = torch.tile(logscales, (1, 3)) # 3. Compute opacities opacities = torch.sigmoid(selectedparams['logitopacities']) # 4. Compute scales scales = torch.exp(logscales) # 5. Normalize rotations rotations = F.normalize(selectedparams['unnormrotations'], p=2, dim=-1) # 6. Initialize means2D means3D = selectedparams['means3D'] means2D = torch.zeroslike(means3D, device=means3D.device) # 7. Construct rendervar for color rendervar = { 'means3D': means3D, 'colorsprecomp': selectedparams['rgbcolors'], 'rotations': rotations, 'opacities': opacities, 'scales': scales, 'means2D': means2D } # 8. Construct rendervar for depth depthrendervar = rendervar.copy() if w2c is not None: # Helper function implementation detail: projects means3D using w2c # to get depth and silhouette values depthrendervar['colorsprecomp'] = getdepthandsilhouette(means3D, w2c) else: # Fallback if w2c not provided, though typically required for depth variant depthrendervar['colorsprecomp'] = torch.zeroslike(means3D) return rendervar, depthrendervar def getdepthandsilhouette(means3D, w2c): # Implementation detail: Projects 3D means to 2D using w2c. # Returns depth values and silhouette mask as a tensor. # This is a placeholder for the specific projection logic defined in the source context. pass Parameters: currtimestep: Integer or float indicating the current time step. Typical values depend on the sequence length. Edge Cases: If logscales has a last dimension of 1, it must be tiled to 3; failure to do so causes shape mismatch in the rasterizer. means2D must be initialized on the same device (CUDA) as means3D. Time Complexity: Linear with respect to the number of active Gaussians N, due to filtering, element-wise operations (sigmoid, exp, normalize), and dictionary construction. Memory Complexity: Linear with respect to N, as it creates new tensors for the output dictionaries. Strengths: Handles temporal sparsity via filtering; ensures numerical stability via normalization and sigmoid/exp conversions. Limitations: Requires w2c for depth rendering variant; relies on specific tensor shapes from the upstream parameter storage. name: Gaussian Rasterization Wrapper
body: The Gaussian Rasterization Wrapper is a high-level Python function that orchestrates the preparation of 3D Gaussian splat parameters and invokes the underlying differentiable rasterization kernel. It handles the transformation of raw Gaussian attributes (means, quaternions, scales, opacities, and spherical harmonics) into the specific tensor formats required by the CUDA/C++ backend, manages camera matrix inversions, and applies post-processing such as mask-based color zeroing. It distinguishes itself from lower-level kernel calls by providing a unified interface for appearance optimization, packed memory layouts, and sparse gradient computation. Inputs: splats: A dictionary or object containing PyTorch tensors for Gaussian parameters. camtoworlds: Camera-to-world transformation matrices. Ks: Camera intrinsic matrices. width, height: Image dimensions. cfg: A configuration object containing flags for optimization strategies (e.g., packed, sparsegrad, antialiased, cameramodel). masks: (Optional) Boolean tensor indicating valid regions. Outputs: rendercolors: Tensor of rendered RGB(A) colors. renderalphas: Tensor of rendered alpha values. info: Dictionary containing metadata and metrics from the rasterization step. Data Structures: Splat Means: Tensor of shape [N, 3], where N is the number of Gaussians. Splat Quaternions: Tensor of shape [N, 4], representing rotation. Splat Scales: Tensor of shape [N, 3], representing the diagonal of the covariance matrix in the exponent. Splat Opacities: Tensor of shape [N], representing transparency. Splat Colors: Tensor of shape [N, C], where C depends on the number of spherical harmonic coefficients. Steps: 1. Extract and Transform Basic Parameters: Extract the raw means and quaternions from the splats dictionary. Compute the effective scales and opacities using activation functions to ensure valid ranges: \text{scales} = \exp(\text{splats}[\text{"scales"}]) \text{opacities} = \sigma(\text{splats}[\text{"opacities"}]) where \sigma is the sigmoid function. 2. Compute Colors: Determine the color representation based on the configuration's appearance optimization setting. If appearance optimization is enabled: Compute colors via the appearance module (app), add base splat colors, and apply the sigmoid function to ensure values are in [0, 1]. Otherwise: Concatenate the zeroth-order (SH0) and higher-order (SHN) spherical harmonic coefficients: \text{colors} = \text{torch.cat}([\text{self.splats}[\text{"sh0"}], \text{self.splats}[\text{"shN"}]], 1) 3. Determine Rasterization Mode: Set the rasterizemode string based on the cfg.antialiased flag. If cfg.antialiased is true, set rasterizemode = "antialiased". Otherwise, set rasterizemode = "classic". 4. Prepare Camera Matrices: Compute the world-to-camera transformation matrices by inverting the provided camera-to-world matrices: \text{viewmats} = \text{torch.linalg.inv}(\text{camtoworlds}) 5. Invoke Rasterization Kernel: Call the underlying rasterization function with the prepared parameters and configuration flags. The call includes: means, quats, scales, opacities, colors viewmats, Ks, width, height packed=self.cfg.packed: Enables packed memory layout optimization. absgrad: Set to self.cfg.strategy.absgrad if the strategy is DefaultStrategy, otherwise False. sparsegrad=self.cfg.sparsegrad: Enables sparse gradients for memory efficiency. rasterizemode: As determined in Step 3. distributed: Set to True if self.worldsize > 1. cameramodel: From self.cfg.cameramodel. withut=self.cfg.withut: Enables upper-triangle computation. witheval3d=self.cfg.witheval3d: Enables 3D evaluation metrics. kwargs: Any additional keyword arguments. 6. Apply Masks (Post-Processing): If masks are provided, zero out the rendered colors where the mask is false: \text{render\colors}[\sim \text{masks}] = 0 Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def gaussianrasterizationwrapper( splats, camtoworlds, Ks, width, height, cfg, masks=None, app=None, worldsize=1): # Step 1: Extract and transform basic parameters means = splats["means"] quats = splats["quats"] scales = torch.exp(splats["scales"]) opacities = torch.sigmoid(splats["opacities"]) # Step 2: Compute colors if cfg.appearanceoptimizationenabled: # Compute colors via app module, add base colors, apply sigmoid # Note: Exact app module logic is implementation-specific; assuming it returns raw colors rawcolors = app.compute(splats) colors = torch.sigmoid(rawcolors + splats["basecolors"]) else: # Concatenate SH0 and SHN coefficients colors = torch.cat([splats["sh0"], splats["shN"]], dim=1) # Step 3: Determine rasterization mode rasterizemode = "antialiased" if cfg.antialiased else "classic" # Step 4: Prepare camera matrices viewmats = torch.linalg.inv(camtoworlds) # Step 5: Invoke Rasterization Kernel absgrad = False if isinstance(cfg.strategy, DefaultStrategy): absgrad = cfg.strategy.absgrad rendercolors, renderalphas, info = rasterization( means=means, quats=quats, scales=scales, opacities=opacities, colors=colors, viewmats=viewmats, Ks=Ks, width=width, height=height, packed=cfg.packed, absgrad=absgrad, sparsegrad=cfg.sparsegrad, rasterizemode=rasterizemode, distributed=worldsize > 1, cameramodel=cfg.cameramodel, withut=cfg.withut, witheval3d=cfg.witheval3d,) # Step 6: Apply masks if masks is not None: rendercolors[~masks] = 0 return rendercolors, renderalphas, info Parameters: cfg.packed: Boolean. Enables packed memory layout optimization in the rasterization kernel. cfg.sparsegrad: Boolean. Enables sparse gradients for memory efficiency. cfg.withut: Boolean. Enables upper-triangle computation in rasterization. cfg.witheval3d: Boolean. Enables 3D evaluation metrics during rasterization. cfg.antialiased: Boolean. Determines if antialiased or classic rasterization mode is used. cfg.cameramodel: String or enum. Specifies the camera model (e.g., pinhole, fisheye) passed to the kernel. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Precision: The use of exp for scales and sigmoid for opacities ensures numerical stability but requires careful initialization to avoid vanishing or exploding gradients. Mask Handling: Masks are applied after rasterization. If masks are not provided, no post-processing occurs. Distributed Training: The distributed flag is automatically set based on worldsize. Ensure the underlying rasterization kernel supports distributed execution if worldsize > 1. Time Complexity: Dominated by the underlying rasterization kernel, which is generally O(N) with respect to the number of Gaussians N, though dependent on image resolution and overlap. Memory Complexity: Depends on the packed and sparsegrad flags. Packed layout reduces memory overhead by avoiding padding. Sparse gradients reduce memory usage during backpropagation for large scenes. Strengths: Unified interface for various optimization strategies (appearance, masks, sparse gradients). Handles camera matrix inversion automatically. Limitations: Relies on the underlying kernel's performance and correctness. Mask application is a post-processing step, which may not be optimal for all use cases. When to Use: When integrating 3D Gaussian Splatting into a PyTorch training loop with specific configuration needs (e.g., sparse gradients, antialiasing). When Not to Use: If maximum raw performance is required without Python overhead, or if custom rasterization logic is needed beyond the wrapper's capabilities. name: Gaussian Splat View of TSDF Band
body: A visualization technique that renders a filtered Truncated Signed Distance Function (TSDF) voxel band as a continuous surface using isotropic Gaussian splats, where one Gaussian is generated per surface voxel. It differs from mesh-based extraction (e.g., marching cubes) by providing a differentiable, continuous representation suitable for real-time interactive visualization, and from raw voxel rendering by smoothing discrete grid artifacts into a coherent surface. Inputs and Outputs: Input: A TSDF voxel band data structure containing voxel centers, colors, weights, and voxel size. Input: iso (float): The iso-threshold for surface extraction. Default: 0.3. Input: minweight (float): The minimum weight threshold to filter out low-confidence voxels. Default: 1.0. Input: scalemult (float): A multiplier for the voxel size controlling Gaussian spread. Default: 1.0. Input: name (string): The name identifier for the splat scene. Default: "/splats". Output: A handle to the rendered splat scene and the count of splats. Returns (None, 0) if no surface voxels are found. Data Structures: The TSDF band is assumed to provide: voxelsize: A scalar float representing the dimension of a single voxel. centers: An array of 3D coordinates for all voxels. colors: An array of RGB values for all voxels. weights: An array of confidence weights for all voxels. Steps: 1. Filter the Band: Apply an iso-threshold and minimum weight threshold to the voxel band to identify surface voxels. This produces a filtered subset of voxels. 2. Extract Data: Retrieve the centers and colors from the filtered voxel band output. 3. Check for Empty: If the number of extracted centers is zero, return (None, 0). 4. Calculate Standard Deviation: Compute the standard deviation (std) for the isotropic Gaussian using the formula: std = voxel\size \times 0.6 \times scale\mult where voxel\size is the dimension of a single voxel, 0.6 is a fixed overlap factor, and scale\mult is the user-adjustable multiplier. 5. Construct Covariance Matrix: For each Gaussian, construct the covariance matrix \Sigma as: \Sigma = std^2 \times I3 where I3 is the 3x3 identity matrix. This results in isotropic covariances. 6. Render: Add the Gaussians to the scene with the calculated centers, covariances, colors, and unit opacities. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import numpy as np def addsplatscene(server, band,, iso=0.3, minweight=1.0, name="/splats", scalemult=1.0): """ Add the filtered band as isotropic gaussian splats. Returns (handle, count). """ # Step 1: Filter the band # Implementation detail: filterband is assumed to be available in the context # It returns a dict with 'centers', 'colors', and potentially 'weights' out = filterband(band, iso=iso, minweight=minweight) centers = out["centers"] colors = out["colors"] # Step 3: Check for empty if len(centers) == 0: return None, 0 # Step 4: Calculate Standard Deviation voxelsize = float(band["voxelsize"]) std = voxelsize 0.6 scalemult # Step 5: Construct Covariance Matrix # Create a 3x3 identity matrix scaled by std^2 covbase = np.eye(3, dtype=np.float32) (std std) # Broadcast to the number of centers numsplats = len(centers) covariances = np.broadcastto(covbase, (numsplats, 3, 3)) # Step 6: Render # Opacities are set to 1.0 for all splats opacities = np.ones((numsplats, 1), dtype=np.float32) handle = server.scene.addgaussiansplats( name, centers=centers, covariances=covariances, rgbs=colors, opacities=opacities,) return handle, numsplats Parameters: iso: Iso-threshold. Default: 0.3. minweight: Minimum weight threshold. Default: 1.0. scalemult: Multiplier for voxel size. Default: 1.0. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: If filtering results in zero voxels, the function returns None for the handle and 0 for the count. The caller must handle this empty state, for example, by displaying a status message indicating that no surface was found. Not given in the sources. This method was introduced in an unofficial commit to the lingbot-map repository, adding a visualization feature to render TSDF bands as Gaussian splats. feat(vis): gaussian-splat view of the TSDF band ( #13), https://github.com/kaylC4/lingbot-map/commit/3db481f0212047782e57b9834492d49455b0106a, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial)

name: FastGS CUDA Rasterizer Forward/Backward Pass
head: CUDA Gaussian Rasterization, Fast Gaussian Splatting, FastGS CUDA Rasterizer, FastGS Rasterization Pipeline, FastGS Rasterizer
body: The FastGS CUDA Rasterizer is a CUDA-accelerated differentiable rasterization method for 3D Gaussians. It extends the original differentiable Gaussian rasterization with support for additional buffers (sampleBuffer, accummetriccounts) and debug modes. It distinguishes itself from standard implementations by using tile-based binning, radix sorting, and bucket-based parallel blending to optimize memory access and compute throughput. Inputs: means3D, colorsprecomp, opacities, scales, rotations, scalemodifier, cov3Dsprecomp, metricmap, viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, imageheight, imagewidth, dc, sh, shdegree, campos, mult, prefiltered, debug, getflag. Outputs: render (image tensor), viewspacepoints (gradient tensor), visibilityfilter (nonzero indices of radii > 0), radii (tensor), accummetriccounts (tensor). GaussianRasterizationSettings: NamedTuple fields: imageheight (int), imagewidth (int), tanfovx (float), tanfovy (float), bg (torch.Tensor), scalemodifier (float), viewmatrix (torch.Tensor), projmatrix (torch.Tensor), shdegree (int), campos (torch.Tensor), mult (float), prefiltered (bool), debug (bool), getflag (bool), metricmap (torch.Tensor). SampleState: Stores bucket-to-tile mappings, tile boundaries (T), and aspect ratios (ar). ImgState: Stores tile ranges, bucket offsets, accumulated alpha, contribution counts (ncontrib, maxcontrib), pixel colors, and scan buffers. BinningState: Stores the sorted point list (pointlist) and unsorted keys/values. GeomState: Stores 2D means (means2D), conic matrices (conicopacity), and clamping flags. 1. Mark visible Gaussians: Launch checkFrustum kernel to test each Gaussian against the view frustum using infrustum, storing results in present array. 2. Preprocess Gaussians: Launch FORWARD::preprocess to transform 3D means to 2D screen space, compute covariances, clamp values, and determine which tiles each Gaussian touches (tilestouched). 3. Compute prefix sums: Use cub::DeviceScan::InclusiveSum on tilestouched to generate pointoffsets, determining the write offset for each Gaussian in the unsorted key/value buffers. 4. Duplicate and Key Generation: Launch duplicateWithKeys kernel. For each visible Gaussian, iterate over touched tiles to generate a 64-bit key (tile ID in upper 32 bits, depth in lower 32 bits) and store the Gaussian index in gaussianvaluesunsorted and keys in gaussiankeysunsorted. 5. Radix Sort: Sort the unsorted keys and values using cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs. The sort range is determined by numrendered (total instances). The bit depth is 32 + bit, where bit is the higher MSB of the total tile count. 6. Identify Tile Ranges: Launch identifyTileRanges kernel. Iterate through the sorted keys. When the tile ID changes from the previous entry, record the end index of the previous tile and the start index of the current tile in ranges array. 7. Bucket Counting: Launch perTileBucketCount kernel. For each tile, calculate the number of buckets needed as (numsplats + 31) / 32, where numsplats is the count of Gaussians in that tile's range. 8. Bucket Offset Calculation: Use cub::DeviceScan::InclusiveSum on bucketcount to generate bucketoffsets, determining the starting memory location for each tile's bucket data in the sample state buffer. 9. Parallel Rendering: Launch FORWARD::render kernel. Pass tile grid, block dimensions, ranges, sorted point list, bucket offsets, and sample state buffers. Each tile blends its Gaussians independently. Focal lengths: focaly = \text{height} / (2.0 \times \tan\fov\y), focalx = \text{width} / (2.0 \times \tan\fov\x). Tile grid dimensions: \text{tile\grid}.x = (\text{width} + \text{BLOCK\X} - 1) / \text{BLOCK\X}, \text{tile\grid}.y = (\text{height} + \text{BLOCK\Y} - 1) / \text{BLOCK\Y}, \text{tile\grid}.z = 1. Block dimensions are \text{BLOCK\X}, \text{BLOCK\Y}, 1. NDC to pixel conversion: \text{pix} = ((v + 1.0) \times S - 1.0) \times 0.5, where v is the NDC coordinate and S is the screen size. Point transformation by 4x3 matrix (rotation + translation): x' = m0 x + m4 y + m8 z + m{12}, y' = m1 x + m5 y + m9 z + m{13}, z' = m2 x + m6 y + m{10} z + m{14}. Point transformation by 4x4 matrix: includes w' = m3 x + m7 y + m{11} z + m{15}. Vector transformation by 4x3 matrix (rotation only): x' = m0 x + m4 y + m8 z, y' = m1 x + m5 y + m9 z, z' = m2 x + m6 y + m{10} z. Vector transformation by 4x3 transpose matrix: x' = m0 x + m1 y + m2 z, y' = m4 x + m5 y + m6 z, z' = m8 x + m9 y + m{10} z. Gradient of normalized vector w.r.t. z component: dnormvdz = (-vx vz dvx - vy vz dvy + (v^2 - vz^2) dvz) / (v^2)^{3/2}, where v^2 = vx^2 + vy^2 + vz^2. Gradient of normalized vector w.r.t. vector components: dnormvdvi = ((v^2 - vi^2) dvi - vi \frac{d}{dvi}(v^2)) / (v^2)^{3/2}. Gradient of normalized 4D vector: dnormvdvi = ((v^2 - vi^2) dvi - vi (v \nabla v)) / (v^2)^{3/2}, where v \nabla v = \frac{d}{dvi}(v^2) summed appropriately. Sigmoid activation: \text{sigmoid}(x) = 1 / (1 + e^{-x}). Frustum culling check: point is in frustum if p{\text{view}}.z > 0.2f. Projected coordinates are computed as p{\text{proj}} = (p{\text{hom}}.xyz / p{\text{hom}}.w) with p{\text{hom}}.w clamped to 0.0000001. Ellipse intersection calculation: h = \text{coord} - pu, \text{sqrt\term} = \sqrt{\text{disc} \times h^2 + t \times \text{coeff}}, result x = (-\text{con\o}.y \times h - \text{sqrt\term}) / \text{coeff} + pv, y = (-\text{con\o}.y \times h + \text{sqrt\term}) / \text{coeff} + pv. Tile bounding box calculation: \text{rect\min} = \min(\text{grid}, \max(0, \text{int}((p - \text{max\radius}) / \text{BLOCK}))), \text{rect\max} = \min(\text{grid}, \max(0, \text{int}((p + \text{max\radius} + \text{BLOCK} - 1) / \text{BLOCK}))). mult: Multiplier for the compact box to control the tile number of each splat. SHC0: Spherical Harmonics coefficient constant, value 0.28209479177387814f. SHC1: Spherical Harmonics coefficient constant, value 0.4886025119029199f. SHC2: Spherical Harmonics coefficients array, values {1.0925484305920792f, -1.0925484305920792f, 0.31539156525252005f, -1.0925484305920792f, 0.5462742152960396f}. SHC3: Spherical Harmonics coefficients array, values {-0.5900435899266435f, 2.890611442640554f, -0.4570457994644658f, 0.3731763325901154f, -0.4570457994644658f, 1.445305721320277f, -0.5900435899266435f}. BLOCKSIZE: Defined as BLOCKX BLOCKY. NUMWARPS: Defined as BLOCKSIZE / 32. Input Validation: Exactly one of SHs or precomputed colors must be provided. Exactly one of scale/rotation pair or precomputed 3D covariance must be provided. Frustum Culling: Uses a near plane threshold of 0.2f. Points behind this are discarded. Homogeneous Division: Near-zero w is handled by adding 0.0000001f to prevent division by zero. Debug Mode: If debug is true, tensors are copied to CPU before CUDA invocation to allow snapshotting on error. Errors save snapshotfw.dump or snapshotbw.dump. Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import torch import math def fastgsforward(means3D, colorsprecomp, opacities, scales, rotations, cov3Dsprecomp, viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, imageheight, imagewidth, bg, scalemodifier, dc, sh, shdegree, campos, mult, prefiltered, debug, getflag, metricmap=None): # 1. Initialize screenspacepoints tensor with shape (numgaussians, 4) and requiresgrad=True screenspacepoints = torch.zeros(means3D.shape[0], 4, requiresgrad=True, device=means3D.device) # 2. Calculate focal lengths from image dimensions and tangent field-of-view focaly = imageheight / (2.0 tanfovy) focalx = imagewidth / (2.0 tanfovx) # 3. Initialize metricmap if None if metricmap is None: metricmap = torch.zeros(imageheight imagewidth, dtype=torch.int, device=means3D.device) # 4. Configure GaussianRasterizationSettings rastersettings = { 'imageheight': imageheight, 'imagewidth': imagewidth, 'tanfovx': tanfovx, 'tanfovy': tanfovy, 'bg': bg, 'scalemodifier': scalemodifier, 'viewmatrix': viewmatrix, 'projmatrix': projmatrix, 'shdegree': shdegree, 'campos': campos, 'mult': mult, 'prefiltered': prefiltered, 'debug': debug, 'getflag': getflag, 'metricmap': metricmap } # 5. Handle Covariance and Color Precomputation if rastersettings.get('computecov3Dpython', False): cov3Dprecomp = computecov3Dfromscalesrotations(scales, rotations) else: cov3Dprecomp = cov3Dsprecomp if rastersettings.get('convertSHspython', False): colorsprecomp = evaluateSHs(dc, sh, shdegree, means3D) else: pass # Sources do not provide Python SH evaluation code # 6. Prepare Args for CUDA Kernel args = ( rastersettings['bg'], means3D, colorsprecomp, opacities, scales, rotations, scalemodifier, cov3Dprecomp, metricmap, viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, imageheight, imagewidth, dc, sh, shdegree, campos, mult, prefiltered, debug, getflag) # 7. Invoke CUDA Kernel renderedimage, radii, accummetriccounts = renderfastgscuda(args) return { 'render': renderedimage, 'viewspacepoints': screenspacepoints, 'visibilityfilter': radii.nonzero().squeeze(), 'radii': radii, 'accummetriccounts': accummetriccounts } def fastgsbackward(gradoutcolor, contexttensors): # 1. Restore saved tensors (colorsprecomp, means3D, scales, rotations, cov3Dsprecomp, radii, dc, sh, geomBuffer, binningBuffer, imgBuffer, sampleBuffer) and rastersettings from context (colorsprecomp, means3D, scales, rotations, cov3Dsprecomp, radii, dc, sh, geomBuffer, binningBuffer, imgBuffer, sampleBuffer) = contexttensors[:12] rastersettings = contexttensors[12] # 2. Restructure backward arguments argsbw = ( rastersettings['bg'], means3D, radii, colorsprecomp, scales, rotations, rastersettings['scalemodifier'], cov3Dsprecomp, rastersettings['viewmatrix'], rastersettings['projmatrix'], rastersettings['tanfovx'], rastersettings['tanfovy'], gradoutcolor, dc, sh, rastersettings['shdegree'], rastersettings['campos'], geomBuffer, contexttensors['numrendered'], binningBuffer, contexttensors['numbuckets'], sampleBuffer, rastersettings['debug']) # 3. Invoke backward kernel to compute gradients for means2D, colorsprecomp, opacities, means3D, cov3Dsprecomp, dc, sh, scales, rotations grads = rasterizegaussiansbackwardcuda(argsbw) return grads def renderfastgscuda(bg, means3D, colorsprecomp, opacities, scales, rotations, scalemodifier, cov3Dsprecomp, metricmap, viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, imageheight, imagewidth, dc, sh, shdegree, campos, mult, prefiltered, debug, getflag): N = means3D.shape[0] # 1. Mark visible Gaussians: checkFrustum kernel # Transform means to view space using 4x3 matrix (rotation + translation) meansview = transformpoint4x3(viewmatrix, means3D) # Check frustum: pview.z > 0.2f infrustum = meansview[:, 2] > 0.2 present = infrustum.int() # 2. Preprocess Gaussians: FORWARD::preprocess kernel # Transform to screen space, compute covariances, clamp, determine tilestouched means2D, conicopacity, tilestouched = preprocessgaussians( means3D, cov3Dsprecomp, opacities, viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, imageheight, imagewidth, scalemodifier) # 3. Compute prefix sums: cub::DeviceScan::InclusiveSum on tilestouched pointoffsets = inclusivesum(tilestouched) # 4. Duplicate and Key Generation: duplicateWithKeys kernel # Generate 64-bit key: (tileid << 32) | depth gaussiankeysunsorted, gaussianvaluesunsorted = duplicatewithkeys( present, tilestouched, pointoffsets, means2D) # 5. Radix Sort: cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs # Sort range determined by numrendered. Bit depth = 32 + MSB(tilecount) numrendered = present.sum() sortedkeys, sortedvalues = radixsortpairs(gaussiankeysunsorted, gaussianvaluesunsorted, numrendered) # 6. Identify Tile Ranges: identifyTileRanges kernel ranges = identifytileranges(sortedkeys) # 7. Bucket Counting: perTileBucketCount kernel # numbuckets = (numsplats + 31) / 32 bucketcount = (ranges.diff() + 31) // 32 # 8. Bucket Offset Calculation: cub::DeviceScan::InclusiveSum on bucketcount bucketoffsets = inclusivesum(bucketcount) # 9. Parallel Rendering: FORWARD::render kernel # Initialize sample buffer state samplechunksize = requiredsizeforbuckets(bucketoffsets[-1] if len(bucketoffsets) > 0 else 0) samplechunkptr = allocatebuffer(samplechunksize) samplestate = SampleState.fromchunk(samplechunkptr, bucketoffsets[-1] if len(bucketoffsets) > 0 else 0) # Determine feature pointer if colorsprecomp is not None: featureptr = colorsprecomp else: featureptr = geomstate.rgb # From geomBuffer # Launch render kernel outcolor = torch.zeros(imageheight, imagewidth, 3, device=means3D.device) radii = torch.zeros(N, device=means3D.device) metricCount = torch.zeros(imageheight imagewidth, device=means3D.device) renderkernel( tilegrid=(imagewidth // BLOCKX, imageheight // BLOCKY, 1), block=(BLOCKX, BLOCKY, 1), ranges=ranges, pointlist=sortedvalues, bucketoffsets=bucketoffsets, samplestate=samplestate, means2D=means2D, featureptr=featureptr, conicopacity=conicopacity, bg=bg, outcolor=outcolor, radii=radii, metricmap=metricmap, getflag=getflag, metricCount=metricCount) return outcolor, radii, metricCount def preprocessgaussians(means3D, cov3Dsprecomp, opacities, viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, imageheight, imagewidth, scalemodifier): # Transform 3D means to view space meansview = transformpoint4x3(viewmatrix, means3D) # Project to NDC using 4x4 matrix meanshom = transformpoint4x4(projmatrix, meansview) # Handle near-zero w by adding 0.0000001f w = meanshom[:, 3] + 1e-7 meansndc = meanshom[:,:3] / w.unsqueeze(1) # NDC to Pixel conversion: pix = ((v + 1.0) S - 1.0) 0.5 pixx = ((meansndc[:, 0] + 1.0) imagewidth - 1.0) 0.5 pixy = ((meansndc[:, 1] + 1.0) imageheight - 1.0) 0.5 means2D = torch.stack([pixx, pixy, meansndc[:, 2]], dim=1) # Compute 2D Covariance and clamp conicopacity = computeconiccovariance(means2D, cov3Dsprecomp, scalemodifier) # Determine tiles touched using tile bounding box calculation BLOCKX = 16 # Example block size BLOCKY = 16 maxradius = computemaxradius(conicopacity) rectmin = torch.clamp((means2D[:,:2] - maxradius) / BLOCKX, min=0).int() rectmax = torch.clamp((means2D[:,:2] + maxradius + BLOCKX - 1) / BLOCKX, max=(imagewidth // BLOCKX)).int() tilestouched = (rectmax - rectmin).sum(dim=1) return means2D, conicopacity, tilestouched def computeconiccovariance(means2D, cov3D, scalemodifier): # Extract 2D submatrix from 3D covariance # Apply scale modifier to opacity # Return conic matrix and scaled opacity pass # Sources do not provide implementation details def computemaxradius(conicopacity): # Ellipse intersection calculation: h = coord - pu # sqrtterm = sqrt(disc h^2 + t coeff) # x = (-cono.y h - sqrtterm) / coeff + pv # y = (-cono.y h + sqrtterm) / coeff + pv # Return max distance pass # Sources do not provide implementation details Time Complexity: Dominated by the radix sort and bucket-based blending. Memory Complexity: Requires buffers for sorted keys/values, tile ranges, bucket offsets, and sample states. Performance: Optimized for high throughput on CUDA-capable GPUs by minimizing memory contention through tile-based binning and radix sorting. Strengths: High rendering speed, differentiable, supports additional metric buffers. Limitations: High memory overhead for large scenes due to sorting and bucketing. The FastGS CUDA Rasterizer is part of the FastGS project, an unofficial extension of 3D Gaussian Splatting. It builds upon the original differentiable Gaussian rasterizer by Inria, adding optimizations for tile-based rendering and additional debugging features. name: GaussianRasterizationSettings
head: 4D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization, GaussianRasterizationSettings configuration, GaussianRasterizer
body: GaussianRasterizationSettings is a configuration structure (typically a NamedTuple or struct) that encapsulates the camera parameters, scene constraints, and rendering flags required to invoke the differentiable 3D Gaussian rasterizer. It solves the problem of translating high-level camera definitions (Field of View, view/projection matrices) and scene properties into the specific numerical formats expected by the underlying CUDA kernel. It differs from the rasterizer itself by handling the setup of state and memory layout rather than the pixel-wise projection and blending logic. Inputs: The rasterizer receives the settings object along with per-Gaussian attributes: means3D: (N, 3) tensor of 3D positions. opacities: (N,) tensor of scalar opacities. scales / rotations: (N, 3) and (N, 4) tensors for scale and quaternion rotation, OR cov3Dprecomp: (N, 6) tensor of pre-computed 3D covariance matrix elements. shs / colorsprecomp: Spherical Harmonics coefficients or pre-computed RGB colors. Camera parameters: viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, campos. Optional dynamic parameters: ts (time), scalest, rotationsr for 4D Gaussians. Outputs: color: Rendered image tensor. radii: Visibility mask for Gaussians. depth: Per-pixel depth. flow: Optional 2D flow field. Gradients for all input attributes. This method initializes the GaussianRasterizationSettings object and prepares auxiliary state tensors required to invoke the differentiable Gaussian rasterizer. It solves the problem of translating high-level camera parameters (Field of View) and scene constraints into the specific numerical formats expected by the CUDA kernel. It differs from the rasterizer itself by handling the setup of state and memory layout rather than the pixel-wise projection and blending logic. The GSCache DiffRasterizer Interface is a C++ class-based abstraction for managing the differentiable rasterization of 3D Gaussians. It encapsulates camera state, frame buffer management, and the forward/backward passes required for gradient-based optimization of Gaussian splatting parameters. It distinguishes itself by providing a unified interface that handles not only rendering but also the integration of optimization steps (densification, pruning) and data access for the Gaussian model parameters. A rasterization technique that represents a 3D Gaussian kernel as two halves split by a plane through its center, allowing distinct opacity values for each half to better represent sharp edges and planar surfaces. The splitting plane normal \mathbf{n} = [n1, n2, n3]^T is a learned unit vector, stored using the three unused normal parameters in the original 3D-GS kernel implementation. Opacity \alpha1 applies where \mathbf{n}^T(\mathbf{x}-\boldsymbol{\mu}) \ge 0, and \alpha2 applies where \mathbf{n}^T(\mathbf{x}-\boldsymbol{\mu}) < 0. This increases memory by only one additional parameter per kernel compared to 3D-GS. Technique to reduce Gaussian footprints and superfluous ray-Gaussian intersections using a generalized kernel exponent and adaptive alpha clamping. The generalized Gaussian kernel is: \exp \left[ -\frac{1}{2n{\text{expo}}} ((x - \mu)^T \Sigma^{-1} (x - \mu))^{n{\text{expo}}} \right] where n{\text{expo}} controls bulkiness. 3DGRT uses 4.5 n{\text{expo}} in the denominator, while GRay uses 1 2^{n{\text{expo}}} to make initialization less sensitive and result in smaller initial Gaussians. Dynamic clamping can cause visible artifacts for large Gaussians, though these are less apparent when using DI since most Gaussians stay small. Time Complexity: Linear in the number of Gaussians N and pixels P, dominated by projection and sorting steps in the CUDA kernel. Memory Complexity: O(N + P) for storing Gaussian attributes and intermediate buffers (geomBuffer, binningBuffer, imgBuffer). Performance: Real-time rendering on modern GPUs (e.g., RTX 4090) for scenes with hundreds of thousands of Gaussians. Strengths: Differentiable, fast, supports dynamic scenes (4D-GS). Limitations: Sensitive to input tensor shapes and device placement; requires careful handling of None values. Originating from the 3D Gaussian Splatting paper, the rasterization settings have been extended to support dynamic scenes in 4D Gaussian Splatting (ICLR 2024). body: This method initializes the GaussianRasterizationSettings object and prepares auxiliary state tensors required to invoke the differentiable Gaussian rasterizer. It solves the problem of translating high-level camera parameters (Field of View) and scene constraints into the specific numerical formats expected by the CUDA kernel. It differs from the rasterizer itself by handling the setup of state and memory layout rather than the pixel-wise projection and blending logic. Inputs: viewpointcamera: An object containing camera properties, specifically FoVx and FoVy (in radians), worldviewtransform, and potentially other metadata. pc: A point cloud or Gaussian object providing getxyz() to determine device and data type. imageheight, imagewidth: Integer dimensions of the target render. bgcolor: Background color tensor. scalemodifier: Float multiplier for Gaussian scales. returndepth: Boolean flag. Outputs: settings: An instance of GaussianRasterizationSettings. screenspacepoints: A tensor initialized to zero, used for gradient accumulation during rasterization. Data Structures: 1. GaussianRasterizationSettings: A configuration object holding: imageheight: int imagewidth: int tanfovx: float (\tan(\text{FoV}x / 2)) tanfovy: float (\tan(\text{FoV}y / 2)) bgcolor: Tensor scalemodifier: float worldviewtransform: Tensor (4x4 matrix) returndepth: bool 2. screenspacepoints: A tensor with shape matching the number of Gaussians, dtype and device matching pc.getxyz(), initialized to zeros. requiresgrad is set to True. Steps: 1. Compute the tangent of half the horizontal and vertical fields of view: \text{tanfovx} = \tan\left(\frac{\text{FoV}x}{2}\right) \text{tanfovy} = \tan\left(\frac{\text{FoV}y}{2}\right) 2. Cast imageheight and imagewidth to integers. 3. Initialize the GaussianRasterizationSettings object with the computed tangents, dimensions, background color, scale modifier, and world view transform. 4. Retrieve the device and data type from the Gaussian positions (pc.getxyz()). 5. Create a screenspacepoints tensor of zeros with the same shape, dtype, and device. 6. Set requiresgrad=True on screenspacepoints. 7. Attempt to call screenspacepoints.retaingrad(). If this fails (e.g., older PyTorch versions), pass silently. Pseudocode: Unverified code. Compute tan(fov/2) tanfovx = math.tan(viewpointcamera.FoVx 0.5) tanfovy = math.tan(viewpointcamera.FoVy 0.5) # 2. Initialize Settings Object settings = GaussianRasterizationSettings( imageheight=int(imageheight), imagewidth=int(imagewidth), tanfovx=tanfovx, tanfovy=tanfovy, bg=bgcolor, scalemodifier=scalemodifier, viewmatrix=viewpointcamera.worldviewtransform, projmatrix=viewpointcamera.fullprojtransform, # Assumed available for completeness, though not explicitly in notes shdegree=pc.activeshdegree, # Assumed available campos=viewpointcamera.cameracenter, # Assumed available prefiltered=False, # Assumed default debug=False, returndepth=returndepth) # 3. Prepare screenspacepoints tensor # Get device and dtype from the Gaussian positions xyz = pc.getxyz() device = xyz.device dtype = xyz.dtype # Initialize to zeros screenspacepoints = torch.zeros( xyz.size(0), 3, # Assuming 3D coordinates for screenspace points device=device, dtype=dtype, requiresgrad=True) # 4. Retain gradients for backward pass try: screenspacepoints.retaingrad() except AttributeError: # Fallback for older PyTorch versions where retaingrad might not be available or necessary in the same way pass return settings, screenspacepoints Parameters: scalemodifier: Multiplier applied to Gaussian scales during rasterization. Default value is 1.0. returndepth: Boolean flag controlling whether depth information is returned alongside the color render. Device Mismatch: Ensure bgcolor and other tensors are on the same device as the Gaussian positions to avoid CUDA errors. Memory Complexity: O(N) for the screenspacepoints tensor, where N is the number of Gaussians. Strengths: Minimal overhead; prepares necessary state for the heavy rasterization kernel. body: This step prepares the scene data and computational buffers required to invoke the differentiable Gaussian rasterizer. It initializes tensors for gradient accumulation and constructs the configuration object that defines the camera parameters and rendering constraints. It differs from the rasterizer itself by handling the setup of state and memory layout rather than the pixel-wise projection and blending logic. The setup process ensures that all necessary tensors are allocated on the correct device with appropriate gradient tracking capabilities, and that the rasterization settings are correctly formatted for the underlying C++/CUDA kernel. Inputs: pc: The Gaussian point cloud object containing attributes (e.g., xyz, scales, rotations, SH coefficients). viewpointcamera: The current camera object containing field of view (FoV) and position. imagewidth, imageheight: The resolution of the target image. background: The background color tensor. Outputs: GaussianRasterizationSettings: An object containing all camera and rendering parameters. screenspacepoints: A tensor initialized to zero, used to store gradients for 2D screen-space means. GaussianRasterizationSettings The settings object aggregates the following fields: imagewidth: Integer, width of the output image. imageheight: Integer, height of the output image. tanfovx: Float, tangent of half the horizontal field of view. tanfovy: Float, tangent of half the vertical field of view. bgcolor: Tensor, background color (must be on GPU). scalemodifier: Float, multiplier for Gaussian scales (default 1.0). viewmatrix: Tensor, 4x4 view transformation matrix. projmatrix: Tensor, 4x4 projection matrix. shdegree: Integer, number of spherical harmonic degrees. campos: Tensor, camera position in world coordinates. Additional fields may include opacity modifiers, depth settings, or time parameters depending on the specific implementation variant. screenspacepoints Shape: (N,) or (N, 2) depending on implementation, where N is the number of Gaussians. Dtype: Same as pc.getxyz().dtype. Device: Same as pc.getxyz().device. Requires Grad: True. 1. Initialize Gradient Tensor: Create a zero tensor screenspacepoints with the same dtype and device as the 3D positions (pc.getxyz()). This tensor is used to store gradients of the 2D screen-space means. 2. Enable Gradient Retention: Call retaingrad() on screenspacepoints to ensure gradients are retained during the backward pass, allowing access to the gradient of the 2D means. 3. Calculate FOV Tangents: Compute the tangent of half the field of view for the x and y axes: \text{tanfovx} = \tan\left(\frac{\text{viewpoint\camera.FoVx}}{2}\right) \text{tanfovy} = \tan\left(\frac{\text{viewpoint\camera.FoVy}}{2}\right) 4. Construct Settings Object: Instantiate GaussianRasterizationSettings with the calculated FOV tangents, image dimensions, background color, scale modifier, view/projection matrices, SH degree, and camera position. Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math import torch def setupgaussianrasterization(pc, viewpointcamera, imagewidth, imageheight, background): """ Prepares tensors and settings for Gaussian rasterization. Args: pc: Gaussian point cloud object with getxyz() method. viewpointcamera: Camera object with FoVx, FoVy, and position. imagewidth: int, width of the output image. imageheight: int, height of the output image. background: Tensor, background color on GPU. Returns: settings: GaussianRasterizationSettings object. screenspacepoints: Tensor for 2D mean gradients. """ # Step 1: Initialize screenspacepoints tensor # Must match dtype and device of 3D positions xyz = pc.getxyz() screenspacepoints = torch.zeros(xyz.shape[0], device=xyz.device, dtype=xyz.dtype, requiresgrad=True) # Step 2: Retain gradients for screenspacepoints # This allows gradient access during backward pass screenspacepoints.retaingrad() # Step 3: Calculate FOV tangents tanfovx = math.tan(viewpointcamera.FoVx 0.5) tanfovy = math.tan(viewpointcamera.FoVy 0.5) # Step 4: Construct GaussianRasterizationSettings # Note: The exact constructor signature may vary by implementation. # Common parameters include: # - image dimensions # - FOV tangents # - background color # - scale modifier (default 1.0) # - view/projection matrices # - SH degree # - camera position settings = GaussianRasterizationSettings( imagewidth=imagewidth, imageheight=imageheight, tanfovx=tanfovx, tanfovy=tanfovy, bgcolor=background, scalemodifier=1.0, # Default value viewmatrix=viewpointcamera.viewmatrix, projmatrix=viewpointcamera.projmatrix, shdegree=pc.shdegree, campos=viewpointcamera.campos) return settings, screenspacepoints scalemodifier: Multiplier for the Gaussian scale. Default is 1.0. bgcolor: Background color tensor. Must be on GPU. Device Mismatch: bgcolor must be on the same device as the Gaussian attributes. Failure to move bgcolor to GPU will cause kernel launch errors. Gradient Loss: If retaingrad() is not called on screenspacepoints, gradients for 2D means will not be accessible during the backward pass, breaking differentiability for certain optimization steps. FOV Calculation: Ensure FoVx and FoVy are in radians if math.tan is used. If they are in degrees, conversion is required. Time Complexity: O(N) for tensor initialization, where N is the number of Gaussians. The FOV calculation is O(1). Memory Complexity: O(N) for screenspacepoints. Strengths: Minimal overhead; prepares necessary state for differentiable rendering. Limitations: Requires careful handling of device placement and gradient retention. It differs from standard rasterization by handling continuous volumetric primitives (Gaussians) via alpha blending, enabling gradient flow through the rendering process for optimization. Inputs and Outputs: Inputs: means3D: (N, 3) tensor of 3D Gaussian centers. colorsprecomp: (N, 3) or (N, C) tensor of precomputed colors. opacities: (N,) tensor of per-Gaussian opacities. scales: (N, 3) tensor of log-scale factors (optional if cov3Dprecomp is provided). rotations: (N, 4) tensor of unit quaternions (optional if cov3Dprecomp is provided). cov3Dprecomp: (N, 6) tensor of precomputed 3D covariance matrix elements (optional if scales/rotations are provided). rastersettings: A GaussianRasterizationSettings object containing camera and rendering parameters. sh: Spherical Harmonics coefficients (optional, used if colorsprecomp is not provided). shdegree: Degree of SH. Outputs: color: (H, W, 3) or (H, W, C) rendered image tensor. radii: (N,) tensor of screen-space radii for visible Gaussians (used for backward pass and culling). If cov3Dprecomp is None, initialize it as an empty tensor. 2. Debug Mode Handling: If rastersettings.debug is True, deep-copy all arguments to the CPU to allow snapshotting for debugging if an exception occurs. 3. Backend Invocation: Invoke the C++/CUDA rasterization routine C.rasterizegaussians (or rasterizegaussians) with the restructured arguments. The arguments passed to the C++ routine include: bg, means3D, colorsprecomp, opacities, scales, rotations, scalemodifier, cov3Dsprecomp, viewmatrix, projmatrix, tanfovx, tanfovy, imageheight, imagewidth, sh, shdegree, campos, prefiltered, debug. 4.
