name: Splat Data Buffer Layout
head: SplatData Layout, Structure-of-Arrays Splat Storage
body: The Splat Data Buffer Layout defines the memory organization for 3D Gaussian primitives in differentiable volume rendering, specifically within the GaussianSet Data Structure family. It solves the problem of efficient GPU rendering by storing per-Gaussian attributes in separate contiguous linear buffers (Structure-of-Arrays, SoA), maximizing cache coherency during rasterization. Unlike sibling methods that focus on coefficient indexing [5570-spherical-harmonics-coefficient-layout.md] or covariance calculation [6840-covariance-splat-reading.md], this layout focuses on the raw storage of learnable parameters (position, scale, rotation, opacity, SH) in a flat, contiguous format suitable for direct memory access by vertex/fragment shaders. Inputs and Outputs: Input: A collection of N Gaussian splats, each defined by position, scale, rotation, opacity, and spherical harmonics coefficients. Output: A set of contiguous FloatBuffer arrays (or equivalent linear memory blocks) for each attribute type. Data Structures: The layout consists of five distinct contiguous buffers, each of size proportional to N: 1. Positions: N \times 3 floats (x, y, z). 2. Scales: N \times 3 floats. The source readScales reads logarithmic scales from splat objects and writes the corresponding linear scale values into the buffer. 3. Rotations: N \times 4 floats representing quaternions in scalar-last order (x, y, z, w). 4. Opacities: N floats. Base layout stores scalar opacity. 5. Spherical Harmonics (SH): N \times D \times 3 floats, where D is the number of coefficients per channel [5570-spherical-harmonics-coefficient-layout.md]. The indexing formula for the c-th channel (c \in \{0,1,2\}) of the d-th coefficient (d \in \{0, \dots, D-1\}) of the i-th splat is: idx = ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + c This layout groups data by splat, then by coefficient index, then by spatial dimension (RGB) [5570-spherical-harmonics-coefficient-layout.md]. Algorithm: The conversion from a high-level object collection to the SoA buffer layout follows these steps: 1. Initialize Buffers: Allocate contiguous float buffers for each attribute type. posbuf: size N \times 3 scalebuf: size N \times 3 rotbuf: size N \times 4 opacitybuf: size N shbuf: size N \times D \times 3 2. Iterate and Extract: For each splat i from 0 to N-1: a. Extract position components (xi, yi, zi) and write to posbuf at indices [3i, 3i+1, 3i+2]. b. Extract scale components (s{x,i}, s{y,i}, s{z,i}) from logarithmic storage and write linear values to scalebuf at indices [3i, 3i+1, 3i+2]. c. Extract rotation quaternion (xi, yi, zi, wi) in scalar-last order and write to rotbuf at indices [4i, 4i+1, 4i+2, 4i+3]. d. Extract opacity \alphai and write to opacitybuf at index i. e. Extract SH coefficients. For each coefficient index d \in \{0, \dots, D-1\} and channel c \in \{0, 1, 2\}: Calculate buffer index: idx = ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + c. Write coefficient value to shbuf at idx. 3. Return Buffers: Return the set of populated buffers. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math from typing import List, Dict def buildsplatbuffers(splats: List['Splat'], shdegree: int) -> Dict[str, List[float]]: """ Converts a list of Splat objects into a Structure-of-Arrays layout. Args: splats: List of N Splat objects. shdegree: Degree of spherical harmonics (D = (degree+1)^2). Returns: Dictionary containing contiguous buffers for positions, scales, rotations, opacities, and spherical harmonics. """ N = len(splats) D = (shdegree + 1) 2 # Initialize buffers positions = [0.0] (N 3) scales = [0.0] (N 3) rotations = [0.0] (N 4) opacities = [0.0] N shcoeffs = [0.0] (N D 3) for i, s in enumerate(splats): # 1. Positions (x, y, z) positions[3 i + 0] = s.getpositionx() positions[3 i + 1] = s.getpositiony() positions[3 i + 2] = s.getpositionz() # 2. Scales (convert log to linear as per source readScales) scales[3 i + 0] = math.exp(s.getscalelogx()) scales[3 i + 1] = math.exp(s.getscalelogy()) scales[3 i + 2] = math.exp(s.getscalelogz()) # 3. Rotations (scalar-last quaternion: x, y, z, w) rotations[4 i + 0] = s.getrotationx() rotations[4 i + 1] = s.getrotationy() rotations[4 i + 2] = s.getrotationz() rotations[4 i + 3] = s.getrotationw() # 4. Opacity opacities[i] = s.getopacity() # 5. Spherical Harmonics # Indexing: ((i D) + d) 3 + c for d in range(D): for c in range(3): idx = ((i D) + d) 3 + c shcoeffs[idx] = s.getshcoefficient(d, c) return { "positions": positions, "scales": scales, "rotations": rotations, "opacities": opacities, "shcoeffs": shcoeffs } Parameters: N: Number of Gaussians. D: Number of SH coefficients per channel, determined by the SH degree. For degree-3, D=16. TideGS defines D=59 as the total learnable parameters per Gaussian (3 pos + 3 scale + 4 rot + 1 opacity + 48 SH). Scale storage: The source reads logarithmic scales from splat objects and writes linear values to the buffer. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Precision: Float32 is standard for buffers. Boundary Conditions: Buffer sizes must be exactly N \times \text{stride}. If N is dynamic, resizing must follow specific growth rules (see Dynamic Gaussian Splatting Scene Management). Quaternion Order: Must be scalar-last (x, y, z, w) as specified in. Using scalar-first will cause incorrect rotation application. SH Indexing: The formula idx = ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + c is critical [5570-spherical-harmonics-coefficient-layout.md]. Deviating from this (e.g., channel-major) breaks compatibility with standard rendering shaders [5570-spherical-harmonics-coefficient-layout.md]. A logical layout for all learnable per-Gaussian attributes stored out-of-core on SSD, organized into contiguous spatial blocks to improve I/O efficiency and spatial locality. It differs from the standard in-memory SoA layout by introducing spatial blocking and Morton sorting to optimize disk reads. Choose this variant for training scenes with billions of Gaussians where memory exceeds GPU capacity. Definition: A unified logical layout \Theta \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D} for all learnable per-Gaussian attributes, stored out-of-core as contiguous block records on SSD. Step: Morton-sort Gaussians by the codes of their centers before blocking to ensure spatially nearby Gaussians map to nearby indices and blocks. Formula: \text{Block}(k):= \Theta[kB: (k+1)B], \quad k \in \{0, \dots, K-1\} where K = \lceil N/B \rceil. Parameter: Block size B=4096. With D=59 parameters (degree-3 SH) and fp32 (4 bytes), each block is 4096 \times 59 \times 4 = 964,544 bytes (236 contiguous 4 KB pages, ~944 KiB). Layout: Logical layout \Theta \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D} with D=59. Stored as contiguous block records on SSD. CPU/GPU materialize only cached/resident blocks. Pitfall: Gaussian centers move during training, changing block bounds. The owner block is fixed (no migration/duplication). Bounds are conservatively refreshed, allowing neighboring block bounds to overlap, but each Gaussian remains uniquely owned and rasterized exactly once. Time Complexity: O(N) to build the buffers from object data. O(1) access to any attribute given the splat index. Memory Complexity: O(N \times D{attr}), where D{attr} is the total number of floats per splat. For degree-3 SH, D{attr} = 3 + 3 + 4 + 1 + 16 \times 3 = 62 floats per splat. Performance: Maximizes GPU cache coherency by ensuring shaders iterate over single attributes without skipping irrelevant data. Strengths: Simple to implement, highly efficient for in-memory rendering, standard compatibility with GPU shaders. Limitations: High memory footprint for large N. When to use: Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering and training where all Gaussians fit in GPU memory. When not to use: Scenes with billions of Gaussians requiring out-of-core optimization (use Unified Parameter Layout and SSD Blocking). The Splat Data Buffer Layout is a foundational component of the 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline, specifically as implemented in libraries like JSplat. It builds on the Structure-of-Arrays paradigm common in graphics programming to optimize data access patterns for parallel rendering. The specific use of scalar-last quaternions aligns with standard practices in differentiable rendering. The SSD blocking variant is used in TideGS for large-scale training. name: Splat Data Encoding & Disabled Splat Detection
head: Disabled Splat Detection, Splat Data Encoding
body: This method defines the binary encoding scheme for 3D Gaussian splats and provides the logic to detect disabled splats during spatial queries and sorting. It solves the problem of efficiently filtering out inactive or merged Gaussians without allocating separate boolean flags or requiring complex metadata lookups. It is distinct from standard active/inactive flags by embedding the status directly into the data payload's bit pattern, allowing the renderer to treat disabled splats as invalid data during coordinate extraction. This builds on Splat Data Buffer Layout. Inputs: A stream of splat data stored in two Uint32Array buffers. Outputs: A boolean indicating if a splat is disabled; modified coordinates (NaN) if disabled. Data Structure: Each splat occupies 32 bytes (8 words), split across two arrays: splatA: Words 0–3 (16 bytes). splatB: Words 4–7 (16 bytes). For splat index i, the starting index in splatB is i4 = i \times 4. Parameters: SPLATBLOCKSDISABLED: A constant used to configure the renderer's block handling mode. Its exact numeric value is not provided in the sources. Disabled Splat Signature: A splat is considered disabled if the following bit pattern is detected in splatB: 1. The upper 16 bits of splatB[i4 + 1] equal 0xfc00. 2. The entire value of splatB[i4 + 2] equals 0xfc00fc00. Algorithm: 1. For each splat index i: a. Calculate i4 = i \times 4. b. Read word1 = splatB[i4 + 1]. c. Read word2 = splatB[i4 + 2]. d. Check if (word1 >> 16) == 0xfc00 AND word2 == 0xfc00fc00. e. If true, the splat is disabled. Coordinate Extraction with Detection: When extracting center coordinates (x, y, z) for sorting or spatial queries: 1. If the splat is disabled, set x = \text{NaN}, y = \text{NaN}, z = \text{NaN}. 2. If the splat is enabled, extract coordinates normally from the encoding. 3. Pass these coordinates to the sorting/spatial query function. Standard NaN-aware sorting or spatial partitioning will exclude these entries. Pitfalls: False Positives: If valid Gaussian data accidentally matches the 0xfc00 pattern, the splat will be incorrectly disabled. Processing Artifacts: If disabled splats are not detected and processed as valid, they may cause rendering artifacts or incorrect sorting behavior because their coordinates are undefined or meaningless. Boundary Checks: Ensure array bounds are respected when accessing splatB[i4 + 1] and splatB[i4 + 2]. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def issplatdisabled(splatB, i): i4 = i 4 word1 = splatB[i4 + 1] word2 = splatB[i4 + 2] return (word1 >> 16) == 0xfc00 and word2 == 0xfc00fc00 def extractcenterwithdisabledcheck(splatA, splatB, i): if issplatdisabled(splatB, i): return (float('nan'), float('nan'), float('nan')) # Not given in the sources. x = decodefloat(splatA[i 4 + 0]) y = decodefloat(splatA[i 4 + 1]) z = decodefloat(splatA[i 4 + 2]) return (x, y, z) def decodefloat(word): import struct return struct.unpack('f', struct.pack('I', word))[0] Time Complexity: O(1) per splat for detection. Memory Overhead: Zero additional memory; the status is encoded within the existing 32-byte splat structure. Performance: Extremely fast detection via bitwise operations. Strengths: Efficient, compact, and integrates seamlessly with NaN-based filtering in spatial data structures. Limitations: Requires strict adherence to the reserved bit pattern; any corruption of the data could lead to false positives or negatives. This method is part of the Gaussian-Splat-Lite renderer, an unofficial implementation of 3D Gaussian Splatting optimized for WebGPU. It was developed to handle large-scale Gaussian datasets efficiently in a browser environment, where memory and performance constraints are significant. The specific encoding and detection mechanism were designed to minimize overhead while ensuring robust handling of merged or inactive Gaussians. name: GpuEdgeCost
head: GPU edge-cost evaluator
body: GpuEdgeCost is a WebGPU compute shader that evaluates the L2 field-error cost for merging pairs of 3D Gaussians, mirroring the logic of the CPU computeEdgeCost function. It enables differentiable inverse volume rendering optimizations by calculating the error introduced when two splats are merged, allowing the system to identify and remove redundant Gaussians. Unlike CPU-based implementations, it utilizes WGSL shaders and storage buffers to handle large datasets in batches, overcoming GPU memory binding limits. Inputs: Splat Data Buffer (splatBuf): Interleaved storage of all splat attributes. Size is maxN SPLATSTRIDE 4 bytes. Neighbor Row Buffer (nbRowBuf): Array of u32 containing neighbor row indices for the current dispatch batch. Size is slotsPerBatch 4 bytes. Uniforms Buffer: Contains slotBase (u32) and slotCount (u32). Host-side Validation: The host must ensure numSplats <= maxN, outCosts length equals nbRows length, and nbRows length is a multiple of k. Outputs: Costs Buffer (outBuf): Array of f32 storing the calculated cost per slot. Size is slotsPerBatch 4 bytes. Splat Storage Layout (Interleaved, Stride SPLATSTRIDE): Each splat occupies SPLATSTRIDE floats. The layout is: [0..2]: Mean position xyz (f32) [3..8]: Covariance matrix \Sigma elements xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz (f32) [9]: Sqrt determinant sqrtDet (f32) [10]: Alpha alpha (f32) [11]: Mass mass (f32) [12..14]: Base color rgb (f32) [15]: Squared norm of base color |base|² (f32) Constants: SPLATSTRIDE: Equal to CACHESTRIDE. SENTINEL: 0xFFFFFFFF (u32), indicating an empty slot. EPSCOV: Small epsilon added to covariance diagonal terms to prevent singularity. PI15: Constant \pi^{1.5}. COLORWEIGHT: Weighting factor for color distance in the final cost. The host manages batching to respect the WebGPU limit of 65,535 workgroups per dimension. Each workgroup contains 64 threads. 1. Batch Setup: Calculate numBatches = ceil(s / slotsPerBatch), where s is the total number of slots. Iterate batch from 0 to numBatches - 1: slotBase = batch slotsPerBatch slotCount = min(slotsPerBatch, s - slotBase) Copy the slice of nbRows from slotBase to slotCount into nbRowBuf. Dispatch the compute shader with slotBase and slotCount in the uniforms buffer. Read slotCount 4 bytes from outBuf into a scratch buffer outScratch. Copy the first slotCount elements from outScratch to outCosts starting at index slotBase. 2. Compute Shader Execution (Per Thread): Each thread processes one dense slot. Get global ID gid.x. Set bid = gid.x. If bid >= uniforms.slotCount, return. Read row = nbRow[bid] from nbRowBuf. If row == SENTINEL, set costs[bid] = 0.0 and return. Calculate offsets: io = ((uniforms.slotBase + bid) / K) SPLATSTRIDE jo = row SPLATSTRIDE. Load Splat i data from splatBuf at io: mui, si (6 elements), sdi, ai, mi, bi, bni. Load Splat j data from splatBuf at jo: muj, sj, sdj, aj, mj, bj, bnj. 3. Merge Calculation: Merge Weights: W = mi + mj pi = select(0.5, mi / W, W > 0.0) pj = 1.0 - pi Merged Mean: mm = pi mui + pj muj di = mui - mm dj = muj - mm Merged Covariance: Calculate sm (6 elements). For diagonal terms (indices 0, 3, 5), add EPSCOV. Example for xx (index 0): sm[0] = pi (di.x di.x + si[0]) + pj (dj.x dj.x + sj[0]) + EPSCOV Similar formulas apply for other elements using corresponding components of di and dj. Merged Determinant: Calculate detm using cofactor expansion of sm. Clamp detm to 1e-30. sqrtDetM = sqrt(detm). Merged Opacity: Compute eigenvalues e = eig3(sm). Scales s0, s1, s2 = sqrt(max(e.x/y/z, 1e-18)). ellipsoidArea = ellipsoidArea(s0, s1, s2). am = min(1.0, W / max(ellipsoidArea, 1e-30)). Color Terms: bij = dot(bi, bj) bim = pi bni + pj bij bjm = pi bij + pj bnj bnm = pi pi bni + 2.0 pi pj bij + pj pj bnj 4. Error Cost Calculation: Self-Interaction Terms: selfI = ai ai bni PI15 sdi selfJ = aj aj bnj PI15 sdj selfM = am am bnm PI15 sqrtDetM Cross-Gaussian Products: cIJ = crossG(sdi, sdj, si+sj, mui-muj) cIM = crossG(sdi, sqrtDetM, si+sm, di) cJM = crossG(sdj, sqrtDetM, sj+sm, dj). Total Error E: E = selfI + selfJ + selfM + 2.0 ai aj bij cIJ - 2.0 ai am bim cIM - 2.0 aj am bjm cJM 5. Final Cost Assembly: Calculate color distance squared: dc2 = bni + bnj - 2.0 bij Clamp dc2 to 0.0 if negative (to handle float noise). costs[bid] = select(E, 0.0, E < 0.0) + COLORWEIGHT select(dc2, 0.0, dc2 < 0.0). The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def gpuedgecostdispatch(nbrows, splatdata, maxn, splatstride, slotsperbatch=4194240): s = len(nbrows) numbatches = (s + slotsperbatch - 1) // slotsperbatch outcosts = [0.0] s # Pre-allocate buffers (conceptual) splatbuf = allocatebuffer(maxn splatstride 4) nbrowbuf = allocatebuffer(slotsperbatch 4) outbuf = allocatebuffer(slotsperbatch 4) # Write splat data once writetobuffer(splatbuf, splatdata) for batch in range(numbatches): slotbase = batch slotsperbatch slotcount = min(slotsperbatch, s - slotbase) # Prepare nbRow buffer for this batch writetobuffer(nbrowbuf, nbrows[slotbase: slotbase + slotcount]) # Dispatch Compute Shader # Uniforms: slotBase=slotbase, slotCount=slotcount # Bindings: splatBuf, nbRowBuf, outBuf dispatchcomputeshader(slotbase, slotcount) # Read results outscratch = readfrombuffer(outbuf, slotcount 4) # Copy to final output for i in range(slotcount): outcosts[slotbase + i] = outscratch[i] return outcosts def computeedgecost(gid, uniforms, nbrow, splatbuf, costs): bid = gid if bid >= uniforms.slotCount: return row = nbrow[bid] if row == 0xFFFFFFFF: # SENTINEL costs[bid] = 0.0 return # Offsets io = ((uniforms.slotBase + bid) / K) SPLATSTRIDE jo = row SPLATSTRIDE # Load Splat i mui = splatbuf[io + 0: io + 3] si = splatbuf[io + 3: io + 9] sdi = splatbuf[io + 9] ai = splatbuf[io + 10] mi = splatbuf[io + 11] bi = splatbuf[io + 12: io + 15] bni = splatbuf[io + 15] # Load Splat j muj = splatbuf[jo + 0: jo + 3] sj = splatbuf[jo + 3: jo + 9] sdj = splatbuf[jo + 9] aj = splatbuf[jo + 10] mj = splatbuf[jo + 11] bj = splatbuf[jo + 12: jo + 15] bnj = splatbuf[jo + 15] # Merge Weights W = mi + mj pi = mi / W if W > 0.0 else 0.5 pj = 1.0 - 2.0 bij dc2 = max(dc2, 0.0) costval = max(E, 0.0) costval += COLORWEIGHT max(dc2, 0.0) costs[bid] = costval Empty Slots: If a neighbor row index is SENTINEL (0xFFFFFFFF), the cost is set to 0.0 and the thread returns early. This prevents reading invalid memory. Float Noise: Negative values resulting from squared norm calculations (e.g., dc2) are clamped to 0.0 to handle floating-point precision errors. NaN/Inf: These are preserved in the calculation to allow the host to detect and fail loudly on degenerate input data. Memory Limits: WebGPU has a maximum storage buffer binding size (typically ~2 GB). To avoid driver-side errors, data is processed in batches (slotsPerBatch) rather than uploading the full N·k slot list at once. The host must check maxStorageBufferBindingSize before buffer creation. Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the number of slots, as each thread processes one slot independently. The batching overhead is O(N / slotsPerBatch) dispatches. Memory Complexity: O(N) for the splat data buffer. The auxiliary buffers (nbRowBuf, outBuf) are sized based on slotsPerBatch, not total N, keeping peak GPU memory usage constant regardless of scene size. Performance: Performance is limited by the WebGPU workgroup limit (65,535 workgroups per dimension), necessitating the batching strategy. Strengths: Efficiently handles large-scale Gaussian splat datasets by offloading the expensive merge-cost calculation to the GPU while managing memory constraints through batching. Limitations: Requires WebGPU support. The batching introduces some host-GPU synchronization overhead for reading/writing buffers. name: Spherical Harmonics Coefficient Layout
head: Per-Dimension SH Storage, SH Buffer Layout
body: This method defines the memory layout for spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients within the Structure-of-Arrays (SoA) data structure of 3D Gaussian Splatting. It solves the problem of efficiently storing and accessing per-gaussian color information by grouping coefficients by splat, then by coefficient index, and finally by RGB channel. It differs from interleaved layouts (which group by channel) by optimizing for sequential access patterns during coefficient evaluation [5570-spherical-harmonics-coefficient-layout.md]. Inputs: N: Number of Gaussians. D: Total number of SH coefficients for the chosen degree, calculated as D = \text{dimensionsForDegree}(shDegree). Source data: A collection of splats, each containing D SH vectors. Outputs: A contiguous linear buffer (e.g., FloatBuffer) of size N \times D \times 3 floats. Data Structure: The buffer is indexed using the formula: idx = ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + c Where: i \in [0, N-1] is the splat index. d \in [0, D-1] is the SH coefficient index. c \in \{0, 1, 2\} represents the RGB channel (0 for Red, 1 for Green, 2 for Blue). Steps: 1. Initialize a buffer of size N \times D \times 3. 2. Iterate over each splat index i from 0 to N-1. 3. For each splat, iterate over each coefficient index d from 0 to D-1. 4. For each coefficient, write the three components to the buffer: Red component at index ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + 0. Green component at index ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + 1. Blue component at index ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + 2. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def writeshcoefficients(buffer, splats, shdimensions): """ Writes SH coefficients into a flat buffer in SoA layout. Args: buffer: A mutable array or buffer of size N shdimensions 3. splats: A list or collection of splat objects. shdimensions: The total number of SH coefficients D for the current degree. """ n = len(splats) for i in range(n): splat = splats[i] for d in range(shdimensions): # Get the base index for this coefficient's RGB triplet baseidx = (i shdimensions + d) 3 # Write R, G, B components buffer[baseidx + 0] = splat.getshx(d) buffer[baseidx + 1] = splat.getshy(d) buffer[baseidx + 2] = splat.getshz(d) Parameters: shDimensions (D): Determined by the SH degree. For degree 0, D=1; for degree 1, D=4; for degree 2, D=9; for degree 3, D=16; for degree 4, D=25. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Degree Mismatch: Ensure shDimensions matches the actual number of coefficients stored in the splat objects. Using an incorrect D will cause buffer overflows or misaligned reads. Precision: Coefficients are stored as 32-bit floats. Quantization methods (e.g., INT8) are separate optimizations. SH Coefficient Interleaving is a data layout strategy that packs SH coefficients into a single contiguous array by grouping coefficients by channel rather than by degree. It solves the problem of efficient memory access during rendering by ensuring that all color channels for a specific SH degree are stored adjacently, which aligns with how SH values are evaluated and applied to RGB output. It differs from the standard layout (which stores all coefficients for one channel before moving to the next) by optimizing for vectorized processing of the RGB triplet during the final color computation step [15882-sh-coefficient-interleaving.md]. This variant manages SH coefficients by storing them in separate GPU textures keyed by block identifiers. The process involves iterating over all SH keys, reusing existing textures, marking them for update if needsUpdate is true, or creating new textures from the source data if they do not exist. This approach is used in streaming contexts to manage memory and update frequency. This variant uses INT8 quantization for spherical harmonics coefficients to reduce memory traffic and bandwidth requirements. It is part of hardware-optimized rendering pipelines that leverage Tensor Cores for acceleration. Memory Complexity: O(N \times D). The storage size is directly proportional to the number of Gaussians and the number of SH coefficients per Gaussian. Access Pattern: Sequential access within a splat's coefficients is efficient. Random access to a specific coefficient requires calculating the index ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + c. Strengths: The layout aligns with the SoA paradigm, allowing efficient bulk transfers and updates. It simplifies the mapping from splat index to coefficient data. Limitations: Not optimized for vectorized RGB operations during rendering compared to interleaved layouts. Requires careful handling of D to avoid misalignment. When to use: Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting implementations where simplicity and compatibility with SoA buffers are prioritized. When not to use: When rendering performance is bottlenecked by memory bandwidth and vectorized RGB processing is critical; consider interleaved layouts or quantized variants. The layout is part of the 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering pipeline, specifically within the data structure management for differentiable volume rendering. It was formalized in the context of efficient GPU-based rendering of Gaussian splats. The specific indexing scheme is documented in unofficial implementations such as JSplat and Gaussian-Splat-Lite. Quantized variants have been explored in recent research for hardware acceleration. name: SH Coefficient Interleaving
head: SH Data Layout Interleaving, SH Interleaving
body: SH Coefficient Interleaving is a data layout strategy for 3D Gaussian Splatting that packs spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients into a single contiguous array by grouping coefficients by channel rather than by degree. It solves the problem of efficient memory access during rendering by ensuring that all color channels for a specific SH degree are stored adjacently, which aligns with how SH values are evaluated and applied to RGB output. It differs from non-interleaved layouts (which store all coefficients for one channel before moving to the next) by optimizing for vectorized processing of the RGB triplet during the final color computation step. Inputs: shdc: A 3-component vector (RGB) representing the zeroth-degree (DC) spherical harmonic coefficients. shrest: A 1D array of floating-point numbers containing the higher-order SH coefficients. The total number of coefficients per channel is coeffsperchannel. The total size of shrest is 3 coeffsperchannel. channels: The number of color channels, typically 3 (RGB). Outputs: result: A 1D array containing the interleaved SH data. The total size is 3 + (3 coeffsperchannel). Data Structure: The output array is structured as follows: 1. The first 3 elements are shdc.x, shdc.y, shdc.z. 2. The remaining elements are filled by iterating through the SH degrees (indices i from 0 to coeffsperchannel - 1). For each degree i, the coefficients for all 3 channels are appended in order: shrest[0 coeffsperchannel + i], shrest[1 coeffsperchannel + i], shrest[2 coeffsperchannel + i]. Algorithm: 1. Initialize an empty list result. 2. Append shdc.x to result. 3. Append shdc.y to result. 4. Append shdc.z to result. 5. Let coeffsperchannel be the number of higher-order coefficients per channel. 6. For i from 0 to coeffsperchannel - 1: a. For j from 0 to 2 (representing R, G, B): i. Calculate the index in the source array: index = j coeffsperchannel + i. ii. Append shrest[index] to result. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def interleaveshcoefficients(shdc, shrest, coeffsperchannel): """ Interleaves SH DC and rest coefficients into a single array. Args: shdc: List or array of 3 floats [R, G, B] for DC coefficients. shrest: List or array of floats containing higher-order SH coefficients. Layout is assumed to be [Rcoeffs..., Gcoeffs..., Bcoeffs...]. coeffsperchannel: Integer, number of higher-order coefficients per channel. Returns: List of floats with interleaved layout. """ result = [] # Append DC coefficients result.append(shdc[0]) result.append(shdc[1]) result.append(shdc[2]) # Interleave rest coefficients # shrest is organized as [R0, R1,..., Rn, G0, G1,..., Gn, B0, B1,..., Bn] # We want to output: R0, G0, B0, R1, G1, B1,... for i in range(coeffsperchannel): for j in range(3): # 0 for R, 1 for G, 2 for B index = j coeffsperchannel + i result.append(shrest[index]) return result Parameters: coeffsperchannel: Determined by the maximum SH degree used. For degree 1, coeffsperchannel = 3. For degree 2, coeffsperchannel = 8. Not given in the sources for other degrees, but standard SH theory applies. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Precision: The source code in implies the use of standard floating-point types (likely f32 or f16 depending on the asset format). Precision loss can occur if converting to lower precision formats like Norm11 or Norm6 without proper quantization. Boundary Conditions: Ensure shrest has exactly 3 coeffsperchannel elements. Accessing shrest[index] where index >= len(shrest) will cause an out-of-bounds error. Degenerate Input: If coeffsperchannel is 0, only the DC coefficients are written. A parallel job that converts raw spherical harmonic coefficients from input splat data into a specific output format (Float32, Float16, Norm11, or Norm6) for storage in a Gaussian Splat asset. Time Complexity: O(N), where N is the total number of SH coefficients. The operation involves a single pass through the shrest array with constant-time appends. Memory Complexity: O(N) for the output array. The input and output arrays are of similar size, so no significant memory overhead is incurred beyond the output buffer. Performance: This layout is optimized for rendering performance. By interleaving RGB coefficients for each SH degree, the GPU can load a single SH degree's contribution for all three color channels in a single memory transaction or vector load, reducing memory bandwidth pressure during the color evaluation phase. Strengths: Efficient memory access patterns for RGB rendering; compact storage. Limitations: Requires careful indexing logic during data preparation. Not optimal for algorithms that process one color channel independently across all degrees. SH Coefficient Interleaving is a specific data layout technique used in modern 3D Gaussian Splatting engines, such as Brush, to optimize the storage and retrieval of spherical harmonic coefficients for view-dependent coloring. It builds on the general principles of spherical harmonic representation in graphics. head: CreateSHDataJob, SH Data Encoding, SH Format Conversion
body: This method converts raw spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients from input splat data into a specific binary format for storage in a Gaussian Splat asset. It supports multiple encoding formats (Float32, Float16, Norm11, Norm6) to balance precision and memory usage. It differs from sibling methods by focusing on the final serialization step into a contiguous byte array, rather than the interleaving of coefficients or the optimization of the splat parameters themselves. Inputs and Outputs: Input: NativeArray<InputSplatData> containing splat data with fields sh1 through shF (15 coefficients per splat). Output: NativeArray<byte> containing the serialized SH data. Format Selector: GaussianSplatAsset.SHFormat enum defining the target encoding. Data Structures: The output is structured as an array of SHTableItem variants, depending on the format: SHTableItemFloat32: Contains 15 float3 fields (sh1 to shF) and one float3 padding field (shPadding). SHTableItemFloat16: Contains 15 half3 fields (sh1 to shF) and one float3 padding field (shPadding). SHTableItemNorm11: Contains 15 uint fields (encoded via EncodeFloat3ToNorm11) and one uint padding field (shPadding). SHTableItemNorm6: Contains 15 uint fields (encoded via EncodeFloat3ToNorm565) and one uint padding field (shPadding). Steps: 1. Determine if clustered SH data is available. If clusteredSHs exists, calculate size as clusteredSHs.Length SizeOf<SHTableItemFloat16>, create a byte array, copy clusteredSHs reinterpreted as bytes, and return. 2. If no clustered data, calculate dataLen using GaussianSplatAsset.CalcSHDataSize(inputSplats.Length, shFormat). 3. Create a NativeArray<byte> data of size dataLen. 4. Instantiate a CreateSHDataJob with mInput, mFormat, and mOutput (the byte array). 5. Schedule the job with job.Schedule(inputSplats.Length, 8192). 6. Complete the job and copy data to a result byte array. 7. Dispose of the NativeArray<byte> and return the result. Job Execution (Parallel Step): For each index in the input array: 1. Read splat = mInput[index]. 2. Switch on mFormat: Float32: Create SHTableItemFloat32 res. Copy splat.sh1 through splat.shF to res.sh1 through res.shF. Set res.shPadding = default. Write res to mOutput[index]. Float16: Cast splat.sh1 through splat.shF to half3. Copy to SHTableItemFloat16. Set shPadding = default. Write to output. Norm11: Encode splat.sh1 through splat.shF using EncodeFloat3ToNorm11. Copy to SHTableItemNorm11. Write to output. Norm6: Encode splat.sh1 through splat.shF using EncodeFloat3ToNorm565. Copy to SHTableItemNorm6. Set shPadding = default. Write to output. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def CreateSHData(inputSplats: NativeArray, shFormat: SHFormat, clusteredSHs: Optional[NativeArray] = None) -> bytes: if clusteredSHs is not None: itemsize = sizeof(SHTableItemFloat16) size = len(clusteredSHs) itemsize result = bytearray(size) # Reinterpret clusteredSHs as bytes and copy for i in range(len(clusteredSHs)): srcbytes = reinterpretasbytes(clusteredSHs[i]) result[iitemsize:(i+1)itemsize] = srcbytes return result datalen = GaussianSplatAsset.CalcSHDataSize(len(inputSplats), shFormat) outputdata = NativeArraybyte job = CreateSHDataJob() job.mInput = inputSplats job.mFormat = shFormat job.mOutput = outputdata # Schedule with batch size 8192 job.Schedule(len(inputSplats), 8192) job.Complete() result = bytearray(outputdata) outputdata.Dispose() return result class CreateSHDataJob: def Execute(self, index: int): splat = self.mInput[index] outputptr = self.mOutput.GetUnsafePtr() if self.mFormat == SHFormat.Float32: res = SHTableItemFloat32() res.sh1 = splat.sh1 res.sh2 = splat.sh2 res.sh3 = splat.sh3 res.sh4 = splat.sh4 res.sh5 = splat.sh5 res.sh6 = splat.sh6 res.sh7 = splat.sh7 res.sh8 = splat.sh8 res.sh9 = splat.sh9 res.shA = splat.shA res.shB = splat.shB res.shC = splat.shC res.shD = splat.shD res.shE = splat.shE res.shF = splat.shF res.shPadding = 0.0 outputptr[index] = res elif self.mFormat == SHFormat.Float16: res = SHTableItemFloat16() res.sh1 = half3(splat.sh1) res.sh2 = half3(splat.sh2) res.sh3 = half3(splat.sh3) res.sh4 = half3(splat.sh4) res.sh5 = half3(splat.sh5) res.sh6 = half3(splat.sh6) res.sh7 = half3(splat.sh7) res.sh8 = half3(splat.sh8) res.sh9 = half3(splat.sh9) res.shA = self.mFormat == SHFormat.Norm11: res = SHTableItemNorm11() res.sh1 = EncodeFloat3ToNorm11(splat.sh1) res.sh2 = EncodeFloat3ToNorm11(splat.sh2) res.sh3 = EncodeFloat3ToNorm11(splat.sh3) res.sh4 = EncodeFloat3ToNorm565(splat.sh9) res.shA = EncodeFloat3ToNorm565(splat.shA) res.shB = EncodeFloat3ToNorm565(splat.shB) res.shC = EncodeFloat3ToNorm565(splat.shC) res.shD = (Float32, Float16, Norm11, Norm6). Batch size for job scheduling: 8192. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Precision loss in Norm11 and Norm6 formats may affect visual quality for high-dynamic-range SH coefficients. The shPadding field must be initialized to default values to ensure memory alignment and avoid undefined behavior in downstream readers. If clusteredSHs is present, the method bypasses the job and assumes Float16 format for the clustered data. Memory Complexity: Linear with respect to the number of splats, O(N), for the output byte array. Performance: The use of a compute job with a batch size of 8192 allows for parallel processing on the GPU, improving performance for large datasets. Strengths: Supports multiple formats for flexibility in precision vs. memory trade-offs. Limitations: The method is specific to the Unity Gaussian Splatting implementation and may not be directly portable to other engines without adaptation. body: Covariance Splat Reading decodes a single 3D Gaussian Splat from two usampler2DArray textures into a CovSplat structure. It retrieves position, color, opacity, and covariance matrix components from GPU texture storage during rendering. Inputs and Outputs: Inputs: index (integer), numSplats (integer), texture1 (usampler2DArray), texture2 (usampler2DArray), splatTexCoord(index) (returns ivec3). Output: covsplat (CovSplat struct). Data Structures: The CovSplat struct contains flags (uint), index (int), rgba (vec4), center (vec3), xxyyzz (vec3), and xyxzyz (vec3). The xxyyzz and xyxzyz fields store the diagonal and off-diagonal elements of the 3×3 covariance matrix, derived from a scale-quaternion representation. Covariance data is stored in two usampler2DArray textures and fetched as two uvec4 values (packed1, packed2). Steps: 1. Initialize covsplat.flags to 0u. 2. Validate index: if index < 0 or index >= numSplats, set covsplat.flags to 0u and return. 3. Compute coord = splatTexCoord(index). 4. Fetch packed1 = texelFetch(texture1, coord, 0). 5. Fetch packed2 = texelFetch(texture2, coord, 0). 6. Decode properties by calling unpackSplatExtCov(packed1, packed2, covsplat.center, covsplat.rgba, covsplat.xxyyzz, covsplat.xyxzyz). 7. Set covsplat.flags to GSPLATFLAGACTIVE if covsplat.xxyyzz and covsplat.xyxzyz are not all zero; otherwise set to 0u. 8. Set covsplat.index = index. Pseudocode: Unverified code. body: Dynamic Gaussian Splatting Scene Management handles the runtime lifecycle of 3D Gaussian splats within a rendering engine, specifically addressing the need for continuous, batched updates in dynamic scenes. Unlike static loading methods that require full re-initialization, this method supports incremental append operations and dynamic buffer resizing, allowing the scene to grow or refresh without restarting the renderer. The method operates on a Structure-of-Arrays (SoA) paradigm, maintaining device-resident buffers for splat attributes and metadata. It manages the transition from host memory to device memory through a series of validated steps. Inputs: shdegree: Integer in [0, 4] determining spherical harmonic complexity. initialcapacity: Integer \ge 0 for the initial buffer size. batchcount: Number of splats to append. meansxyz: N \times 3 float array of positions. quaternionswxyz: N \times 4 float array of rotations in scalar-last order (x, y, z, w). logscalesxyz: N \times 3 float array of log-scales. opacitylogits: N float array of opacity logits. featuresdcrgb: N \times 3 float array of DC spherical harmonic coefficients. featuresshrgb: N \times D \times 3 float array of higher-order SH coefficients, where D = (sh\degree + 1)^2 - 1. cameraparams: Width, height, view matrix (4 \times 4), and intrinsics (fx, fy, cx, cy). scalemodifier: Positive finite float for global scale adjustment. Outputs: Rendered image buffers (RGBA8, Depth, or Opacity). Updated scene state (count, capacity, device buffers). The core state is held in DeviceScene and HostRender structures. DeviceScene (Device Memory): means: float3 pointer, size capacity \times 3. quats: float4 pointer, size capacity \times 4. scales: float3 pointer, size capacity \times 3. opacities: float pointer, size capacity. featuresdc: float3 pointer, size capacity \times 3. featuressh: float3 pointer, size capacity \times num\sh. count: int64t, current number of splats. capacity: int64t, current buffer capacity. shdegree: int, current SH degree. numsh: int, number of SH coefficients per splat. HostRender (Pinned Host Memory): rgb: float3 pointer, size rgb\pixels. scalar: float pointer, size scalar\pixels. rgbpixels: sizet. scalarpixels: sizet. 1. Initialize Renderer: Validate shdegree in [0, 4] and initialcapacity \ge 0. Reset engine state and release existing scene data. Set scene.shdegree to shdegree. Calculate scene.numsh as (sh\degree + 1)^2 - 1. Reserve memory for initialcapacity. Bind scene to engine. 2. Reserve Scene Capacity: If requestedcapacity > currentcapacity: Calculate nextcapacity as \max(requested, \max(4096, current\capacity \times 2)). Grow all device buffers (means, quats, scales, opacities, featuresdc) to nextcount. If numsh > 0, grow featuressh to nextcount numsh. Update scene.capacity and bind scene. 3. Bind Scene to Engine: Set state.curnumsplats to scene.count. Set state.maxnumsplats to scene.capacity. Set state.numsh to scene.numsh and state.shdegree to scene.shdegree. Create DeviceVector views for means, quats, scales, opacities, featuresdc with size capacity. If numsh > 0, create DeviceTensor2D view for featuressh with dimensions (capacity, numsh, 3); else empty tensor. Set state.world.initialized to true if capacity > 0. 4. Append Splats: Validate batchcount \ge 0 and input arrays are non-null. Check for integer overflow: if scene.count > numericlimits<int64t>::max() - batchcount, throw std::overflowerror. Calculate offset = scene.count. Reserve space for offset + batchcount (triggering capacity growth if needed). Copy means, quats, scales, opacities, featuresdc from host to device at offset. If numsh > 0, copy featuressh from host to device at offset numsh. Increment scene.count. 5. Set Camera: Validate width/height > 0 and viewmatrix/intrinsics non-null. Initialize distcoeffs[8] to zero internally. Call setcameraparams with width, height, "PINHOLE", "NONE", viewmatrix (1 \times 4 \times 4 float), and intrinsics (1 \times 4 float). Set width, height, and cameraready = true. 6. Set Scale Modifier: Validate modifier > 0 and finite. If modifier equals current scalemodifier, return. Calculate logdelta = \log(requested\modifier / scale\modifier). Calculate numel = scene.count \times 3. Allocate device scratch buffer of size maxchunk (1 \ll 20). Loop over numel in chunks: Copy logdelta to device chunk. Call floataddinto on scales chunk and device delta chunk. Free scratch buffer. Update scalemodifier. 7. Render Color: Validate output buffer size \ge pixelcount \times 4. If scene.count == 0, fill output with black (RGB 0,0,0) and alpha 255. Determine rendershdegree as \min(requested\sh\degree, scene.sh\degree) if requested \ge 0, else scene.shdegree. Call forward3dgs("3dgs", rendershdegree, true). Get RGB buffer from state.fwd.renders. Resize host.rgb if needed. Copy RGB from device to host. Write RGB to output buffer using writegrayorrgb. 8. Render Depth: Validate output. If scene.count == 0, fill black/alpha 255. Call forward3dgs. Get depth buffer from state.fwd.renders (index 1). Resize host.scalar if needed. Copy depth from device to host. Call writedepth(output, pixelcount). 9. Render Opacity: Validate output. If scene.count == 0, fill black/alpha 255. Call forward3dgs. Get transmittance buffer from state.fwd.renderTs. Resize host.scalar if needed. Copy transmittance from device to host. Loop over pixels to write opacity. Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math import numpy as np class DynamicGaussianScene: def init(self, shdegree: int, initialcapacity: int): self.shdegree = shdegree self.numsh = (shdegree + 1) 2 - 1 self.count = 0 self.capacity = 0 self.scalemodifier = 1.0 # Device buffers (simulated as numpy arrays for clarity) self.means = None self.quats = None self.scales = None self.opacities = None self.featuresdc = None self.featuressh = None self.resize(initialcapacity) def resize(self, newcapacity: int): """Grow buffers to newcapacity following the doubling strategy.""" if newcapacity > self.capacity: nextcapacity = max(newcapacity, max(4096, self.capacity 2)) else: nextcapacity = self.capacity if nextcapacity == self.capacity: return # Grow buffers self.means = np.resize(self.means, (nextcapacity, 3)) self.quats = np.resize(self.quats, (nextcapacity, 4)) self.scales = np.resize(self.scales, (nextcapacity, 3)) self.opacities = np.resize(self.opacities, (nextcapacity,)) self.featuresdc = np.resize(self.featuresdc, (nextcapacity, 3)) if self.numsh > 0: self.featuressh = np.resize(self.featuressh, (nextcapacity, self.numsh, 3)) self.capacity = nextcapacity def append(self, count: int, means: np.ndarray, quats: np.ndarray, logscales: np.ndarray, opacities: np.ndarray, featuresdc: np.ndarray, featuressh: np.ndarray): """Append a batch of splats.""" if count < 0: raise ValueError("Batch count must be >= 0") # Overflow check if self.count > np.iinfo(np.int64).max - count: raise OverflowError("Scene count overflow") offset = self.count self.resize(offset + count) # Copy data to device (simulated by numpy slice assignment) end = offset + count self.means[offset:end] = means self.quats[offset:end] = quats self.scales[offset:end] = logscales self.opacities[offset:end] = opacities self.featuresdc[offset:end] = featuresdc if self.numsh > 0: self.featuressh[offset:end] = featuressh self.count = end def setscalemodifier(self, modifier: float): """Apply global scale modifier via log-space addition.""" if modifier <= 0 or not math.isfinite(modifier): raise ValueError("Modifier must be positive and finite") if modifier == self.scalemodifier: return logdelta = math.log(modifier / self.scalemodifier) self.scalemodifier = modifier # Apply to existing scales in log space using chunked scratch buffer simulation numel = self.count 3 maxchunk = 1 << 20 for i in range(0, numel, maxchunk): chunksize = min(maxchunk, numel - i) # Simulate floataddinto on scales chunk and devicedelta chunk self.scales[i // 3: (i + chunksize) // 3] += logdelta def render(self, width: int, height: int, viewmatrix: np.ndarray, intrinsics: np.ndarray, outputmode: int): """Render the scene.""" pixelcount = width height if self.count == 0: # Fill black/alpha 255 return np.zeros((pixelcount, 4), dtype=np.uint8) # Determine SH degree # In a real implementation, this calls forward3dgs # Here we simulate the result based on mode if outputmode == 0: # Color # Simulate RGB output return np.random.randint(0, 255, (pixelcount, 3), dtype=np.uint8) elif outputmode == 1: # Depth # Simulate Depth output return np.random.rand(pixelcount).astype(np.float32) elif outputmode == 2: # Opacity # Simulate Opacity output return np.random.rand(pixelcount).astype(np.float32) else: raise ValueError("Unknown output mode") shdegree: Integer, range [0, 4]. Determines spherical harmonic complexity. numsh is calculated as (sh\degree + 1)^2 - 1. scalemodifier: Float, must be positive and finite. Applied multiplicatively to splat scales via log-space addition to avoid precision issues and allow dynamic adjustment. Empty Scene: If scene.count == 0 during render, the renderer outputs a black image (RGB 0,0,0) with full alpha (255) instead of crashing or rendering nothing. Buffer Overflow: Append checks for integer overflow when adding batchcount to scene.count. Throws std::overflowerror if scene.count > numericlimits<int64t>::max() - batchcount. Precision: Scales are stored in log-space to ensure positivity during optimization. Linear scales are recovered via s{linear} = \exp(s{log}) for covariance calculation. Manages the dynamic lifecycle of 3D Gaussian splats within a ROS2-enabled rendering pipeline, bridging sensor or simulation data to the GPU renderer. It solves the problem of real-time scene updates by queuing incoming Gaussian batches and efficiently draining them to the renderer state. It differs from static loading by enabling continuous, batched updates via ROS2 communication, allowing the scene to grow or refresh without full re-initialization. Time Complexity: Append operations are O(N) for data copy, where N is the batch size. Capacity growth involves reallocation and copy, which is amortized O(1) per splat if the doubling strategy is used. Rendering is O(P \cdot N) where P is pixel count and N is splat count, typical for Gaussian Splatting. Memory Complexity: O(N \cdot C) where N is capacity and C is the number of attributes per splat. The doubling strategy ensures memory usage is at most 2 \times the required capacity. Performance: The method uses pinned host memory for readback and device buffers for storage, optimizing data transfer. The use of log-space for scales and opacities avoids precision issues during optimization. Strengths: Supports dynamic scenes with incremental updates. Efficient buffer management with minimum capacity of 4096 and doubling strategy. Limitations: Requires careful management of buffer sizes to avoid excessive reallocation. Integer overflow checks are necessary for large scenes. The method originates from the ROSplat project, which integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting with ROS2 for dynamic scene management. It builds on the principles of Structure-of-Arrays (SoA) data layout for cache coherency. body: This method manages the dynamic lifecycle of 3D Gaussian splats within a rendering pipeline, bridging incoming data to the GPU renderer. It solves the problem of real-time scene updates by queuing incoming Gaussian batches and efficiently draining them to the renderer state. It differs from static loading by enabling continuous, batched updates without full re-initialization. Inputs and Outputs: Input: ROS2 messages (SingleGaussian, GaussianArray) containing Gaussian attributes; configuration parameters for scene capacity and rendering options. Output: Updated GPU device memory (DeviceScene) containing Gaussian attributes; rendered images (color, depth, opacity) based on current camera and scene state. Data Structures: The core state is held in DeviceScene and managed via TorchTensorView wrappers. DeviceScene layout: float3 means: Device pointer to position data. Size: capacity 3 floats. float4 quats: Device pointer to rotation quaternions. Size: capacity 4 floats. float3 scales: Device pointer to scale vectors. Size: capacity 3 floats. float opacities: Device pointer to opacity values. Size: capacity floats. float3 featuresdc: Device pointer to DC spherical harmonic coefficients. Size: capacity 3 floats. float3 featuressh: Device pointer to higher-order SH coefficients. Size: capacity numsh 3 floats (if numsh > 0). int64t count: Current number of active Gaussians. int64t capacity: Maximum allocated Gaussians. int shdegree: Active SH degree. int numsh: Number of SH coefficients per Gaussian. TorchTensorView layout: uint64t pointer: Raw device pointer address. int itemsize: Element size in bytes (always sizeof(float)). std::vector<int64t> shape: Dimensions of the tensor. Numbered Steps: 1. ROS Message Conversion: If input is SingleGaussian: Extract xyz (1x3), rotation (1x4), scale (1x3), opacity (1x1, normalized by dividing by 255.0), and sphericalharmonics (1xN). If input is GaussianArray: Validate all messages have identical SH dimension shdim. If shdim == 0, raise ValueError. Allocate arrays of shape (count, 3), (count, 4), (count, 3), (count, 1), (count, shdim). Fill arrays by iterating messages. Pack data into a batch structure compatible with appendgaussians. 2. Batch Queuing: Acquire pendinglock. If refresh flag is true: Clear pendingbatches, set gaussiancount to batchcount, and assign batch to gaussianset. Else (append mode): Calculate available = MAXGAUSSIANS - gaussiancount. If available <= 0, return (drop batch). If batchcount > available, truncate batch to available elements across all fields. Increment gaussiancount by batchcount. Append (batch, refresh) to pendingbatches. Set fullscenedirty = False and havenewgaussians = True. 3. Renderer State Update (drainpending): Get list of pending batches and clear deque. For each (batch, refresh) pair: If batch is None and refresh is true, call gaussrenderer.resetgaussians(). Otherwise, call gaussrenderer.appendgaussians(batch, refresh=refresh). If no pending batches but fullupdate or fullscenedirty is true: If gaussianset is None or empty, call resetgaussians(), else call updategaussiandata(gaussianset, fullupdate=True). Apply scalemodifier, renderoutput, shdegree, modeltransform, camerapose, cameraintrin, and renderresolution to the renderer. Set fullscenedirty = False and havenewgaussians = bool(pendingbatches). 4. Scene Binding (bindscene): Update engine state with scene.count, scene.capacity, scene.numsh, scene.shdegree. Bind device pointers to state.world using TorchTensorView: means via view1d(scene.means, scene.capacity, 3), quats via view1d(scene.quats, scene.capacity, 4), scales via view1d(scene.scales, scene.capacity, 3), opacities via view1d(scene.opacities, scene.capacity, 1), featuresdc via view1d(scene.featuresdc, scene.capacity, 3), and featuressh via view2d(scene.featuressh, scene.capacity, scene.numsh, 3) (if numsh > 0, else empty tensor). Set state.world.initialized = scene.capacity > 0. 5. Rendering: Validate output buffer size (pixelcount 4). If scene.count == 0: Fill output with black (RGB=0, A=255). Determine rendershdegree: min(requestedshdegree, scene.shdegree) if requestedshdegree >= 0, else scene.shdegree. Call forward3dgs("3dgs", rendershdegree, true). Based on outputmode: Color copies RGB from render buffer, Depth copies depth buffer, Opacity computes opacity = 1.0 - transmittance and writes as grayscale or RGB. Parameters: MAXGAUSSIANS: 50,000,000. timescale: 5.0 (camera translation speed multiplier). modeltransformspeed: 100.0 (model translation speed multiplier). scalemodifier: Positive finite float, default 1.0. requestedshdegree: -1 or in [0, 4]. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Null Pointers: append throws if any required array (means, quats, etc.) is null. Buffer Overflow: Output buffer must be at least pixelcount 4 bytes. SH Dimension: shdim == 0 raises ValueError during batch validation. Scale Modifier: Must be positive and finite; uses chunked memory updates (max chunk 1 << 20) for efficiency. body: A method to load 3D Gaussian splats from a ROS topic by subscribing to a SplatArray message and converting the wire format into a GPU-ready SplatGPU struct layout. It differs from static loading by enabling real-time scene updates via ROS2 communication, bridging simulation or sensor data directly into the Gaussian Splatting renderer. Inputs: A ROS2 SplatArray message containing a list of splats, each with pose, opacity, covariance, and spherical harmonics. Outputs: A LoadResult structure containing a vector of SplatGPU structs and the scene's SH degree. Data Structures: SplatGPU: The internal GPU-ready representation. center[3]: float array for position (x, y, z). alpha: float for opacity, normalized to [0, 1]. covA[3]: float array storing the first row of the symmetric 3 \times 3 covariance matrix. covB[3]: float array storing the second row of the symmetric 3 \times 3 covariance matrix. sh[numcoefs][4]: float array for spherical harmonics coefficients where sh[k][0..2] stores RGB for degree k and sh[k][3] is padding. LoadResult: splats: std::vector<SplatGPU>. shdegree: uint32t. Wire Format Mapping: The input SplatArray message contains individual splat messages. The mapping from ROS message fields to SplatGPU fields is as follows: center: Extracted from s.pose.pose.pose.position.x/y/z. alpha: Extracted from s.opacity (uint8, range 0–255) via alpha = opacity / 255.0. covA: Extracted from s.pose.pose.covariance (6x6 row-major array) at indices 0, 1, 2. covB: Extracted from s.pose.pose.covariance at indices 7, 8, 14. sh: Extracted from s.sphericalharmonics (coef-major, RGB-interleaved) where sh[k][0..2] maps to sphericalharmonics[3k+0..2]. Algorithm: 1. Initialize LoadResult out. 2. Determine shdegree: If msg.splats is not empty, set shdegree = msg.splats[0].harmonicsdeg. Else, set shdegree = 0. 3. Calculate numcoefs = (shdegree + 1)^2. 4. Reserve memory for out.splats based on msg.splats.size(). 5. For each splat s in msg.splats: a. Create SplatGPU g. b. Set g.center[0] = (float)s.pose.pose.pose.position.x. c. Set g.center[1] = (float)s.pose.pose.pose.position.y. d. Set g.center[2] = (float)s.pose.pose.pose.position.z. e. Set g.alpha = (float)s.opacity / 255.0f. f. Extract covariance from s.pose.pose.covariance array (let this be cov): i. g.covA[0] = (float)cov[0]. ii. g.covA[1] = (float)cov[1]. iii. g.covA[2] = (float)cov[2]. iv. g.covB[0] = (float)cov[7]. v. g.covB[1] = (float)cov[8]. vi. g.covB[2] = (float)cov[14]. g. Loop k from 0 to numcoefs - 1: i. g.sh[k][0] = (float)s.sphericalharmonics[3k + 0]. ii. g.sh[k][1] = (float)s.sphericalharmonics[3k + 1]. iii. g.sh[k][2] = (float)s.sphericalharmonics[3k + 2]. iv. g.sh[k][3] = 0.0f. h. Push g to out.splats. 6. Set out.shdegree = shdegree. 7. Return out. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. class SplatGPU: def init(self): self.center = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] self.alpha = 0.0 self.covA = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] self.covB = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] self.sh = [] class LoadResult: def init(self): self.splats = [] self.shdegree = 0 def loadrossplats(msg): out = LoadResult() if len(msg.splats) > 0: out.shdegree = msg.splats[0].harmonicsdeg else: out.shdegree = 0 numcoefs = (out.shdegree + 1) 2 for s in msg.splats: g = SplatGPU() g.center[0] = float(s.pose.pose.pose.position.x) g.center[1] = float(s.pose.pose.pose.position.y) g.center[2] = float(s.pose.pose.pose.position.z) g.alpha = float(s.opacity) / 255.0 cov = s.pose.pose.covariance g.covA[0] = float(cov[0]) g.covA[1] = float(cov[1]) g.covA[2] = float(cov[2]) g.covB[0] = float(cov[7]) g.covB[1] = float(cov[8]) g.covB[2] = float(cov[14]) g.sh = [[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0] for in range(numcoefs)] shdata = s.sphericalharmonics for k in range(numcoefs): baseidx = 3 k g.sh[k][0] = float(shdata[baseidx + 0]) g.sh[k][1] = float(shdata[baseidx + 1]) g.sh[k][2] = float(shdata[baseidx + 2]) g.sh[k][3] = 0.0 out.splats.append(g) return out Parameters: QoS Profile: reliable() transport and transientlocal() durability. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Assumes uniform harmonicsdeg across all splats in the message. Assumes deg <= 3. If sphericalharmonics length does not match 3 \times (deg+1)^2, behavior is undefined.
